label: def:regular-curve
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:regular-curve}
A compact curve \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a regular
\(C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\) curve if
$
 \Gamma=\Phi([a,b]),
$
where \(\Phi\) is parametrized by arc length,
\(\Phi\in C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}([a,b];\mathbb R^n)\), and \(\Phi\) is one-to-one,
apart from the possible equality \(\Phi(a)=\Phi(b)\) when the curve is
closed.  Thus
$
 |\Phi'(t)|=1,
 \ t\in[a,b].
$
In the closed case, we also require
\(\Phi'(a)=\Phi'(b)\), and we regard \(\Phi\) as a regular
\(C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\) embedding of
\(\mathbb R/(b-a)\mathbb Z\).  The derivative modulus is then computed using
the cyclic distance on this parameter circle.

title: Proof
body_md:
For $k\geq0$ and $2^{-k-1}<t\leq2^{-k}$, monotonicity gives \(\vartheta(2^{-k-1}) \leq \vartheta(t) \leq \vartheta(2^{-k})\). Integration with respect to $dt/t$ and summation in $k$ give
\eqref{eq:dyadic-Dini}.  To obtain \eqref{eq:dilated-Dini}, choose an
integer $m_c$ such that $c\leq2^{m_c}$.  The terms with $k\leq m_c$ are
bounded by $(m_c+1)\vartheta(1)$, and the remaining sum is bounded by a
shift of the sum in \eqref{eq:dyadic-Dini}.

label: lem:Taylor-Dini
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Taylor-Dini}
Let $F\in C^1(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R^n)$.  If $|x-y|\leq1$, then \(|F(y)-F(x)-DF(x)(y-x)| \leq |x-y|\,\vartheta_F(|x-y|)\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the fundamental theorem of calculus,
\[
F(y)-F(x)-DF(x)(y-x)
 =\int_0^1\bigl(DF(x+t(y-x))-DF(x)\bigr)(y-x)\,dt.
\]
The norm of the integrand is at most
$\vartheta_F(|x-y|)|x-y|$.

label: lem:graph-modulus
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:graph-modulus}
Let \(\Gamma:[c,d]\to\mathbb R^n\) be parametrized by arc length.  Suppose,
after a rotation, that
\[
 \Gamma_1'(s)\geq c_0>0,
 \qquad c\leq s\leq d.
\]
Write \(u=\Gamma_1(s)\), and let \(\Gamma(s)=(u,g(u))\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:graph-modulus}
 \vartheta_g(r)
 \leq C_{c_0}\vartheta_\Gamma(C_{c_0}r),
 \qquad
 0<r\leq C_{c_0}^{-1}.
\end{equation}
In particular, \(g\in C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\) whenever
\(\Gamma\in C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since \(u'(s)=\Gamma_1'(s)\geq c_0\), the inverse function
\(s=s(u)\) satisfies \(|s(u)-s(v)|\leq c_0^{-1}|u-v|\). Moreover, \(g'(u) =\frac{\Gamma_\perp'(s(u))}{\Gamma_1'(s(u))}\). The denominators are at least \(c_0\), and
\(|\Gamma'(s)|=1\).  Hence \(|g'(u)-g'(v)| \leq C_{c_0} |\Gamma'(s(u))-\Gamma'(s(v))| \leq C_{c_0} \vartheta_\Gamma(c_0^{-1}|u-v|)\). Choose \(C_{c_0}\geq\max\{1,c_0^{-1}\}\) large enough that the
preceding estimate has the form in \eqref{eq:graph-modulus}.  If
\(0<r\leq C_{c_0}^{-1}\), then \(C_{c_0}r\leq1\), so the argument of
\(\vartheta_\Gamma\) lies in its defining interval \([0,1]\).
This proves \eqref{eq:graph-modulus}.  For
\(C_{c_0}^{-1}\leq r\leq1\), we have
\(\vartheta_g(r)\leq2\|g'\|_\infty\).  A change of variables on the
remaining part of the Dini integral proves the last assertion.

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \(g(t_0)=0\) and \eqref{eq:local-smallness}, \(\|g\|_{L^\infty(I^*)} \leq \varepsilon_0|I^*|\). Condition \eqref{eq:fixed-collar} gives
\(\rho\in C_c^\infty(I^*)\) such that \(\rho=1\) on
\(\widehat I\) and \(\|\rho'\|_\infty\leq C_\kappa|I^*|^{-1}, \quad \|\rho''\|_\infty\leq C_\kappa|I^*|^{-2}\). Extend $\rho g$ by zero outside $I^*$ and put
$\widetilde g=\rho g$.  Then \(\widetilde g'=\rho g'+\rho'g\). The preceding bounds for \(g\), \(g'\), and \(\rho'\) give
\eqref{eq:extension-slope}.  If $|s-t|\leq r$, the difference of the first
term is bounded by \(\vartheta_g(r)+C\varepsilon_0 r/|I^*|\). The difference of the second term has the same bound, by the estimates
for $\rho'$, $\rho''$, $g$, and $g'$.  If one point lies outside
$I^*$, insert the intervening endpoint of $I^*$; both the extension
and its derivative vanish near that endpoint.  This proves the
estimate in \eqref{eq:extension-modulus} when \(0<t<|I^*|\).
When \(t\geq|I^*|\), \eqref{eq:extension-slope} gives \(\vartheta_{\widetilde g}(t) \leq2\|\widetilde g'\|_\infty \leq C_\kappa\varepsilon_0\). Combining these two ranges proves \eqref{eq:extension-modulus}.  Its
Dini integral is finite by
\eqref{eq:Dini}.

label: lem:annular-A2
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(s=n-\alpha\).  We first prove the Euclidean assertion.  For an
ordinary cube \(Q\), recall that
\[
 \mathcal P^\alpha(Q,\nu)
 =
 \int_{\mathbb R^n}
 \left(
 \frac{\ell(Q)}
 {(\ell(Q)+|y-c_Q|)^2}
 \right)^s d\nu(y).
\]
The forward one-tailed condition with a hole is
\[
 \mathcal A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)
 =
 \sup_Q
 \frac{\omega(Q)}{\ell(Q)^s}
 \mathcal P^\alpha(Q,\mathbf 1_{Q^c}\sigma).
\]

Set \(\delta=(16\sqrt n)^{-1}\), and partition \(\mathbb R^n\) into half-open
cubes \(Q_m\) of side length \(\delta r\).  Let \(Q_m^*\) be the cube
concentric with \(Q_m\) and of side length \(8r\).

Fix \(x\in Q_m\).  If \(r/2<|x-y|\leq2r\), then \(y\notin3Q_m\).
Indeed, \(x\in Q_m\) and \(y\in3Q_m\) would give \(|x-y|\leq2\sqrt n\,\delta r=\frac r8\). Also, \(|y-c_{Q_m}| \leq |y-x|+|x-c_{Q_m}| <2r+\frac r{32}<4r\), so \(y\in Q_m^*\).  Consequently, \(\{y:r/2<|x-y|\leq2r\} \subset E_m:=Q_m^*\setminus3Q_m\). In particular, \(E_m\subset Q_m^c\).

For \(y\in E_m\), we have
\(|y-c_{Q_m}|\leq4\sqrt n\,r\).  Hence
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal P^\alpha(Q_m,\mathbf 1_{Q_m^c}\sigma)
 &\geq
 \mathcal P^\alpha(Q_m,\mathbf 1_{E_m}\sigma)
 \geq
 \left(
 \frac{\delta r}
 {(\delta r+4\sqrt n\,r)^2}
 \right)^s
 \sigma(E_m)
 \geq c_{n,\alpha}r^{-s}\sigma(E_m).
\end{align*}
Since \(\ell(Q_m)=\delta r\), the forward one-tailed condition gives \(r^{-2s}\omega(Q_m)\sigma(E_m) \leq C_{n,\alpha}\mathcal A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)\).

By Cauchy--Schwarz, for \(x\in Q_m\),
\[
 |\mathcal M_{\alpha,r}(f\sigma)(x)|^2
 \leq
r^{-2s}\sigma(E_m)\int_{E_m}|f|^2\,d\sigma.
\]
It follows that
\begin{align*}
 \int_{Q_m}|\mathcal M_{\alpha,r}(f\sigma)|^2\,d\omega
 &\leq
r^{-2s}\omega(Q_m)\sigma(E_m)
 \int_{E_m}|f|^2\,d\sigma
 \leq
C_{n,\alpha}\mathcal A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)
 \int_{Q_m^*}|f|^2\,d\sigma.
\end{align*}
The cubes \(Q_m^*\) have bounded overlap.  Summing in \(m\) proves the
forward estimate.  Interchanging \(\sigma\) and \(\omega\) proves the
dual estimate, using \(\mathcal A_2^{\alpha,*}(\sigma,\omega)\).

We now prove the quasicube assertion.  Let \(L\geq1\) be a common
biLipschitz constant for \(\Omega\) and \(\Omega^{-1}\).  Use the same
partition \(\{Q_m\}\) in the preimage coordinates, and put \(H_m=\Omega Q_m,\quad H_m^*=\Omega Q_m^*,\quad F_m=H_m^*\setminus\Omega(3Q_m)\). If \(x\in H_m\) and \(r/2<d_\Omega(x,y)\leq2r\), the preceding
Euclidean calculation applied to \(\Omega^{-1}x\) and
\(\Omega^{-1}y\) gives \(y\in F_m\).  Also \(F_m\subset H_m^c\).

Write \(c_{H_m}=\Omega(c_{Q_m})\) and
\(a_{H_m}=|H_m|^{1/n}\).  BiLipschitz continuity gives \(L^{-1}\delta r\leq a_{H_m}\leq L\delta r\). For \(y\in F_m\), \(|y-c_{H_m}| \leq L|\Omega^{-1}y-c_{Q_m}| \leq4L\sqrt n\,r\). The quasicube reproducing Poisson integral is
\[
 \mathcal P^\alpha(H,\nu)
 =
 \int_{\mathbb R^n}
 \left(
 \frac{|H|^{1/n}}
 {\bigl(|H|^{1/n}+|y-c_H|\bigr)^2}
 \right)^s d\nu(y).
\]
Therefore \(\mathcal P^\alpha(H_m,\mathbf 1_{H_m^c}\sigma) \geq c_{n,\alpha,L}r^{-s}\sigma(F_m)\). The forward quasicube one-tailed condition gives \(r^{-2s}\omega(H_m)\sigma(F_m) \leq C_{n,\alpha,L}\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)\). Cauchy--Schwarz now gives
\[
 \int_{H_m}
 |\mathcal M_{\alpha,r}^{\Omega}(f\sigma)|^2\,d\omega
 \leq
C_{n,\alpha,L}\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)
 \int_{H_m^*}|f|^2\,d\sigma.
\]
The sets \(H_m^*\) have the same overlap multiplicity as the cubes
\(Q_m^*\), because \(\Omega\) is one-to-one.  Summing in \(m\) proves
the quasicube estimate.  The dual quasicube estimate follows by
interchanging the two measures.  The half-open partition assigns every
boundary atom to one member, and \(F_m\subset H_m^c\) separates the two
measures in each one-tailed product.

label: lem:cutoff-stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cutoff-stability}
Let \(\Psi\) be globally biLipschitz.  Let
\(\chi\in C^\infty([0,\infty))\) satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-near-cutoff}
 0\leq\chi\leq1,\qquad
 \chi=1\text{ on }[0,r_0],\qquad
 \chi=0\text{ on }[2r_0,\infty),\qquad
 |\chi'|\leq C/r_0.
\end{equation}
Fix a measure pair \((\mu,\nu)\) with
\(\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\mu,\nu)<\infty\).  Suppose that
\(K\) satisfies \(|K(x,y)|\leq C_K|x-y|^{\alpha-n}\). Then the operators with kernels \(q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|)K(x,y),\quad q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)(1-\chi(|x-y|))K(x,y)\) have norm at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cutoff-stability-bound}
C\left(\mathfrak N_K^s(\mu,\nu)
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}\right)
\end{equation}
from \(L^2(\mu)\) to \(L^2(\nu)\), uniformly in
\(0<\varepsilon<R\).  Here \(C\) depends on
\(n,\alpha,C_K\) and the biLipschitz constant of \(\Psi\), but not on
\(\varepsilon,R\).  For any fixed family \(\mathcal F\), the
corresponding forward and dual testing bounds hold with
\(\mathfrak N_K^s\) in \eqref{eq:cutoff-stability-bound} replaced by
\(\mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^s\) and
\(\mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^{s,\mathrm{dual}}\), respectively.
For a fixed globally biLipschitz map \(\Omega\), the same assertions hold
with \(\mathfrak A_2^\alpha\) replaced by the combined
\(\Omega\)-quasicube constant.  The testing family may be any
fixed family of bounded Borel sets; in the application it is a family of
\(\Omega\)-quasicubes.  The constant may depend on \(\Omega\).
head: environment

label: eq:q-s-general-kernel
title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(L\) be a common biLipschitz constant for \(\Psi,\Psi^{-1}\).  Then \(L^{-1}|x-y|\leq|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|\leq L|x-y|\). The two cutoff families satisfy
\begin{align*}
 \{q_{\varepsilon,R}\neq s_{\varepsilon,R}\}
 &\subset
 \left\{\frac{\varepsilon}{2L}<|x-y|<L\varepsilon\right\}\cup
 \left\{\frac{R}{L}<|x-y|<2LR\right\}.
\end{align*}
Each set on the right is a union of at most \(C_L\) dyadic annuli.
The size estimate for \(K\) and \cref{lem:annular-A2} therefore give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q-s-general-kernel}
 \sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \bigl\|T_{\varepsilon,R,\mu}^{K,q}
       -T_{\varepsilon,R,\mu}^{K,s}\bigr\|_{L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\nu)}
 \leq C_L C_K\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}.
\end{equation}

It remains to insert \(\chi\).  Put \(\rho=\min\{R,r_0\}\).  If
\(\varepsilon<\rho\), then \(s_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|) -s_{\varepsilon,\rho}(x,y)\) is supported in
\(\{r_0\leq|x-y|\leq2r_0\}\).  If
\(\varepsilon\geq\rho\), then necessarily \(\rho=r_0\), and
\(s_{\varepsilon,R}\chi\) is supported in
\(\{r_0/2<|x-y|<2r_0\}\).  In both cases the error is either zero or is
supported where \(|x-y|\approx r_0\).  Its kernel is bounded by a fixed
number of kernels of the form \(C\rho_0^{\alpha-n} \mathbf 1_{\{\rho_0/2<|x-y|\leq2\rho_0\}}, \quad \rho_0\approx r_0\). Hence
\begin{align*}
 &\sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \left\|\int q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|)
K(x,y)f(y)\,d\mu(y)\right\|_{L^2(\nu)}\leq C\left(\mathfrak N_K^s(\mu,\nu)
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}\right)
 \|f\|_{L^2(\mu)}.
\end{align*}
The full \(q\)-truncation is controlled by
\eqref{eq:q-s-general-kernel}; more precisely,
\[
 \sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \|T_{\varepsilon,R,\mu}^{K,q}\|_{L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\nu)}
 \leq \mathfrak N_K^s(\mu,\nu)
 +C_LC_K\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}.
\]
Subtracting the part with \(\chi\)
gives the same estimate for the part with \(1-\chi\).

For forward testing, apply these identities to \(f=\mathbf 1_E\), restrict
the result to \(E\), and divide by \(\mu(E)^{1/2}\).  The source-radial
term is bounded by \(\mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^s\).  Every annular error
is bounded by its operator norm and hence by
\(C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\).  Interchanging the variables proves
the dual testing estimate.

For the \(\Omega\)-quasicube assertion, use the preimage distance
\(|\Omega^{-1}x-\Omega^{-1}y|\).  By biLipschitz continuity, each
Euclidean annulus above is contained in a fixed number of annuli for
this distance, with comparable radii.  Apply the quasicube form of
\cref{lem:annular-A2} to these annuli.  The preceding proof is otherwise
unchanged.

label: lem:tangent-smooth-comparison
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tangent-smooth-comparison}
Let \(K\) be the fractional Riesz vector \(\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}\), one of
its scalar components \(K_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y) :=e_j\cdot\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(x,y), \quad 1\leq j\leq n\), the conformal fractional Riesz vector \(\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\), or one
of its scalar components \(K_{\Psi,j}^{\alpha,n}(x,y) :=e_j\cdot\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y), \quad 1\leq j\leq n\), where \(\Psi\) is globally biLipschitz.
Let \(\mu,\nu\) be locally finite positive Borel measures, possibly
with common point masses.  Let \(\Omega\) be a fixed globally
biLipschitz map, and compute the combined Muckenhoupt constant with
respect to the \(\Omega\)-quasicubes.  Then
\[
 \sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \left\|
T_{\varepsilon,R,\mu}^{K,\mathrm{tl}}
 -T_{\varepsilon,R,\mu}^{K,s}
 \right\|_{L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\nu)}
 \leq
C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}.
\]
The same estimate holds for the adjoint after interchanging
\(\mu\) and \(\nu\); for a vector kernel, the adjoint is taken
componentwise.  Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak N_K^s
 &\leq C\left(
 \mathfrak N_K^{\mathrm{tl}}
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha}\right),
 &\qquad
 \mathfrak N_K^{\mathrm{tl}}
 &\leq C\left(
 \mathfrak N_K^s
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For every family \(\mathcal F\) of bounded Borel sets, the same two
inequalities hold with
\((\mathfrak N_K^s,\mathfrak N_K^{\mathrm{tl}})\) replaced by either
\[
 (\mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^s,
   \mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^{\mathrm{tl}})
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 (\mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^{s,\mathrm{dual}},
   \mathfrak T_{K,\mathcal F}^{\mathrm{tl},\mathrm{dual}}).
\]
The constant depends only on \(n,\alpha\), the fixed function
\(\eta_0\), and the biLipschitz constants of \(\Omega\) and, in the
conformal case, \(\Psi\).  It is independent of
\(\varepsilon,R,\mu,\nu\), and \(\mathcal F\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Both kernels satisfy \(|K(x,y)|\leq C|x-y|^{-d}, \quad x\neq y\). For the conformal kernel this follows from \(|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|\geq \operatorname{Lip}(\Psi^{-1})^{-1}|x-y|\). Set \(r=|x-y|\).  On
\(\varepsilon\leq r\leq R\), both truncation multipliers are one.
If \(0<r<\varepsilon\), then \(\left| \bigl(t_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y) -s_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\bigr)K(x,y) \right| \leq C\varepsilon^{-d}\). Indeed, the tangent-line term is bounded by
\(C\rho_{\varepsilon,R}^{\alpha}(r)\leq C\varepsilon^{-d}\).
The smooth term vanishes for \(r\leq\varepsilon/2\), while for
\(\varepsilon/2<r<\varepsilon\) it is bounded by
\(Cr^{-d}\leq C\varepsilon^{-d}\).

Let \(A_d=\max\{2,1+d^{-1}\}\). For \(r>R\), both truncated kernels vanish when \(r\geq A_dR\), and
on \(R<r<A_dR\) their difference is bounded by \(CR^{-d}\).
It follows that
\[
 \left|
 \bigl(t_{\varepsilon,R}-s_{\varepsilon,R}\bigr)(x,y)K(x,y)
 \right|
 \leq C\varepsilon^{-d}\mathbf 1_{\{0<|x-y|<\varepsilon\}}
 +CR^{-d}\mathbf 1_{\{R<|x-y|<A_dR\}}.
\]

For the first term, write
\[
 \{0<|x-y|\leq\varepsilon\}
 =
 \bigcup_{j=0}^{\infty}
 \left\{
 2^{-j-1}\varepsilon<|x-y|
 \leq2^{-j}\varepsilon
 \right\}.
\]
On the \(j\)-th annulus, \(\varepsilon^{-d} = 2^{-jd}(2^{-j}\varepsilon)^{-d}\). The quasicube form of \cref{lem:annular-A2} therefore gives a bound
\[
C\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}2^{-jd}
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}
 \leq
C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\mu,\nu)}.
\]
The outer region \(R<|x-y|<A_dR\) is the union of a number of dyadic
annuli depending only on \(d\).  Another application of
\cref{lem:annular-A2} gives the same bound for the outer term.

To use the quasicube version of that lemma, take the annuli in the
preimage distance \(|\Omega^{-1}x-\Omega^{-1}y|\). The biLipschitz inequalities for \(\Omega\) place each Euclidean
annulus above in a fixed number of preimage annuli with comparable
radii.  The factors \(2^{-jd}\) in the inner sum change only by a
fixed constant.

For a vector kernel, take the Euclidean norm before applying the
positive annular majorants.  This proves the vector-valued operator
estimate.  For every \(j\),
\[
 |K_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|\leq|\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|,
 \qquad
 |K_{\Psi,j}^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|
 \leq|\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|.
\]
The same annular majorants therefore prove the scalar estimates, with
constants independent of \(j\).  Since the multipliers are symmetric
in \(x,y\), the same proof applies to the vector or scalar adjoint after
the measures are interchanged.

Let \(E\in\mathcal F\).  Apply the operator estimate to
\(\mathbf 1_E\), restrict the result to \(E\), and divide by
\(\mu(E)^{1/2}\).  This proves the forward testing comparison.
Interchanging \(\mu,\nu\) proves the dual comparison.  This argument
applies to every family of bounded Borel sets, including
\(\Omega\)-quasicubes.

label: prop:change-variable
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:change-variable}
Let \(\Psi\) be as in \eqref{eq:graph-change}.  Assume that \(\Psi\) is
globally biLipschitz.  Let \(\sigma\) and \(\omega\) be locally finite
positive Borel measures with arbitrary supports, possibly with common
point masses.  Let \(\mathcal F\) be a family of bounded
Borel sets.  Then
\begin{align*}
 &\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}(\sigma,\omega)
   +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)}
\approx
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega)
   +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)}.
\end{align*}
The forward and dual testing constants over
\(\mathcal F\) and \(\Psi^{-1}\mathcal F\) satisfy the corresponding
comparisons.  All constants are uniform in the truncation parameters.
For any \(r_0>0\) with \(2r_0\leq1\), put
\begin{equation*}
 \Lambda_{\psi,r_0}
 :=\vartheta_\psi(2r_0)
 +\int_0^{2r_0}\vartheta_\psi(t)\,\frac{dt}{t}
 +\frac{\|\psi\|_\infty}{r_0}.
\end{equation*}
The Taylor and far-field kernel errors are bounded by
\(C\Lambda_{\psi,r_0}\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\).  The cutoff
comparisons add \(C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\).  Thus the full
additive error is bounded by
\(C(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0})\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\).
In these additive estimates, \(C\) depends only on \(n,\alpha\),
the biLipschitz constant of \(\Psi\), and \(\|D\psi\|_\infty\).
The constants in the norm and testing comparisons may also depend on
\(\Lambda_{\psi,r_0}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(p=n+1-\alpha\).  The pullback of the Riesz kernel is \(\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y) := c_{\alpha,n} \frac{\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)} {|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|^p}\). Fix \(r_0>0\) with \(2r_0\leq1\), and choose \(\chi\) as in
\eqref{eq:fixed-near-cutoff}.
Write \(\chi(x,y)=\chi(|x-y|)\).
All kernel identities below are for \(x\neq y\).  As above, every
truncated kernel is defined to be zero on the diagonal.

Since \(\Psi=I+u\), we have
\begin{align}
 \mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)
 &=\chi(x,y)D\Psi(x)\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)
 +(1-\chi(x,y))\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)
 +\mathbf E_{x,\mathrm{near}}(x,y)+\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}(x,y),
 \label{eq:near-decomposition}
\end{align}
where
\begin{align*}
 \mathbf E_{x,\mathrm{near}}(x,y)
 &=c_{\alpha,n}\chi(x,y)
 \frac{u(y)-u(x)-Du(x)(y-x)}
 {|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|^p},\\
 \mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}(x,y)
 &=c_{\alpha,n}(1-\chi(x,y))
 \frac{u(y)-u(x)}{|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|^p}.
\end{align*}
Expansion at \(y\) gives the analogous identity with \(D\Psi(y)\) and
\[
 \mathbf E_{y,\mathrm{near}}(x,y)
 =c_{\alpha,n}\chi(x,y)
 \frac{u(y)-u(x)-Du(y)(y-x)}{|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|^p}.
\]
Since \(\Psi\) is biLipschitz, \cref{lem:Taylor-Dini} gives, for
\(z=x,y\),
\begin{align*}
 |\mathbf E_{z,\mathrm{near}}(x,y)|
 &\leq C|x-y|^{\alpha-n}\vartheta_\psi(|x-y|)
 \mathbf 1_{\{|x-y|\leq2r_0\}},\\
 |\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}(x,y)|
 &\leq C\|u\|_\infty |x-y|^{\alpha-n-1}
 \mathbf 1_{\{|x-y|\geq r_0\}}.
\end{align*}

For \(j\in\mathbb Z\) with \(j\leq1\), the coefficient of
\(|x-y|^{\alpha-n}\) in the near error on the annulus \(2^{j-1}r_0<|x-y|\leq2^jr_0\) is at most \(C\vartheta_\psi(2^jr_0)\).  For \(j\in\mathbb Z\) with
\(j\geq0\), the corresponding coefficient in the far error is at most
\(C\|u\|_\infty/(2^jr_0)\).  Hence
\cref{lem:dyadic-Dini,lem:annular-A2} gives, for \(z=x,y\),
\begin{align}
 &\left\|\int q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)
 \bigl(\mathbf E_{z,\mathrm{near}}(x,y)+\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}(x,y)\bigr)
f(y)\,d\widetilde\sigma(y)\right\|_{L^2(\widetilde\omega)}
\leq
C\Lambda_{\psi,r_0}\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 \|f\|_{L^2(\widetilde\sigma)}.
 \label{eq:uniform-error-operator}
\end{align}
The constant is independent of the supports of the measures and of
\(\varepsilon,R\).
Here we use the quasicube form of \cref{lem:annular-A2} with
\(\Omega=\Psi^{-1}\).  A Euclidean annulus is contained in a fixed
number of \(\Psi^{-1}\)-quasiannuli at comparable radii.  The combined
Muckenhoupt constant is then replaced by the original one using
\eqref{eq:A2-pullback}.

More generally, if \(F\) and \(\Omega\) are globally biLipschitz, then
the combined pullback estimate is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A2-pullback}
 \mathfrak A_{2,F^{-1}\circ\Omega}^\alpha
   (F^*\sigma,F^*\omega)
 \approx
 \mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\sigma,\omega).
\end{equation}
For $H=\Omega Q$ and $\widetilde H=F^{-1}H$, the masses of
corresponding sets agree, and $\widetilde H^c=F^{-1}(H^c)$.
Moreover, $c_{\widetilde H}=F^{-1}(c_H)$ and
$|\widetilde H|^{1/n}\approx|H|^{1/n}$.  BiLipschitz continuity
therefore compares the reproducing Poisson kernels after the change
of variables.  This proves the forward and dual one-tailed comparisons
for these corresponding families.  The common atoms and their masses
also correspond, so the two punctured constants compare as well.
Taking the suprema gives \eqref{eq:A2-pullback}.

By \eqref{eq:uniform-radial-norms}, the cutoff in
\(\mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q\) is radial in the original
variables \(X=\Psi(x)\) and \(Y=\Psi(y)\).  The cutoff in
\(\mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^s\) uses the distance \(|x-y|\).
Let \(L\geq1\) be a common biLipschitz constant for
\(\Psi\) and \(\Psi^{-1}\).  Then
\begin{align}
 \{q_{\varepsilon,R}\neq s_{\varepsilon,R}\}
 &\subset
 \left\{\frac{\varepsilon}{2L}<|x-y|<L\varepsilon\right\}
 \cup
 \left\{\frac{R}{L}<|x-y|<2LR\right\}.
 \label{eq:target-source-cutoff-support}
\end{align}
Indeed, both inner cutoff factors vanish below
\(\varepsilon/(2L)\) and equal one above \(L\varepsilon\).  Both outer
cutoff factors equal one below \(R/L\) and vanish above \(2LR\).

Since \(|\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)|\leq C|x-y|^{\alpha-n}\), each set on the right side of
\eqref{eq:target-source-cutoff-support} is the union of at most
\(C_L\) dyadic annuli.  Hence
\cref{lem:annular-A2} and \eqref{eq:A2-pullback} give
\begin{align}
 &\sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \left\|\int
 (q_{\varepsilon,R}-s_{\varepsilon,R})(x,y)
 \mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)f(y)\,
d\widetilde\sigma(y)\right\|_{L^2(\widetilde\omega)}
 \leq
C_L\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)}
 \|f\|_{L^2(\widetilde\sigma)}.
 \label{eq:target-source-truncation}
\end{align}
The same estimate holds for the adjoint and for both normalized testing
constants.

We also need a fixed upper cutoff.  Put \(\rho=\min\{R,r_0\}\).  If
\(\varepsilon<\rho\), then \(s_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|) -s_{\varepsilon,\rho}(x,y)\) is supported in \(\{r_0\leq|x-y|\leq2r_0\}\).  If
\(\varepsilon\geq\rho\), then \(\rho=r_0\), and
\(s_{\varepsilon,R}\chi\) is supported in
\(\{\rho/2<|x-y|<2\rho\}\).  Another application of
\cref{lem:annular-A2} gives the required bound for the source-radial
cutoff.  The difference between that cutoff and
\(q_{\varepsilon,R}\) is controlled by
\eqref{eq:target-source-truncation}.  More explicitly, if \(T_a\)
denotes the operator with kernel
\(a(x,y)\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)\), then, uniformly in
\(0<\varepsilon<R\),
\begin{align*}
 \|T_{q_{\varepsilon,R}\chi}\|
 &\leq \|T_{s_{\varepsilon,R}\chi}\|
     +C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 \leq \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^s
     +C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 \leq \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
     +C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}.
\end{align*}
The first and last inequalities use
\eqref{eq:target-source-truncation}.  The middle inequality uses the
two cases above and \cref{lem:annular-A2}.  Consequently,
\begin{align}
 &\sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \left\|\int
q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|)
 \mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)f(y)\,
d\widetilde\sigma(y)\right\|_{L^2(\widetilde\omega)}
 \notag\\
 &\qquad\leq C\left(
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)}\right)
 \|f\|_{L^2(\widetilde\sigma)}.
 \label{eq:fixed-upper-pullback}
\end{align}
This estimate also holds for the adjoint.  Repeating the preceding three
inequalities with each operator norm replaced by its normalized testing
expression proves the forward and dual testing estimates.

Multiplying \eqref{eq:near-decomposition} by
\(q_{\varepsilon,R}\), we obtain
\begin{align*}
q_{\varepsilon,R}\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}
 &=D\Psi(x)q_{\varepsilon,R}\chi\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}
 +q_{\varepsilon,R}(1-\chi)\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}+q_{\varepsilon,R}
 (\mathbf E_{x,\mathrm{near}}+\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}).
\end{align*}
The matrix \(D\Psi(x)\) depends only on the left variable.  Thus
we apply the quasicube form of \cref{lem:cutoff-stability} with
\(\Omega=\Psi^{-1}\).  Equation \eqref{eq:A2-pullback} bounds its
combined quasicube constant by
\(C\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega)\).  The lemma and
\eqref{eq:uniform-error-operator} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:one-direction-change}
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
 \leq C\left(
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^s
 +(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0})
   \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\right).
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison}, the source-radial norm on the
right is bounded by the tangent-line norm plus
\(C\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\).  Repeating the preceding inequalities
with each operator norm replaced by its normalized testing expression
proves forward testing.  Expansion at \(y\) proves dual testing because
\(D\Psi(y)\) then depends only on the left variable for the adjoint.
The error in both estimates is
\(C(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0})\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\).  In both
testing estimates, the left-hand side uses the \(q\)-cutoffs, while the
first term on the right-hand side uses the \(s\)-cutoffs.  Equation
\eqref{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison} gives the testing
constants.

For the reverse inequality, we use the following identity for a graph
shear: \(Du(x)^2=0\). Consequently, \((I-\chi(x,y)Du(x))(I+\chi(x,y)Du(x))=I\). Equation \eqref{eq:near-decomposition} is \(\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}} =(I+\chi Du(x))\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n} +\mathbf E_{x,\mathrm{near}}+\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}\). It follows that
\begin{align}
 \mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}
 &=\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}-\chi Du(x)\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}
 -(I-\chi Du(x))
 (\mathbf E_{x,\mathrm{near}}+\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}}).
 \label{eq:reverse-kernel-identity}
\end{align}
Multiply \eqref{eq:reverse-kernel-identity} by
\(q_{\varepsilon,R}\).  The first term is one of the truncations used in
\(\mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q\).  For the second term,
\[
q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|)
Du(x)\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)
 =Du(x)\bigl[q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\chi(|x-y|)
 \mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)\bigr].
\]
Equations \eqref{eq:target-source-truncation} and
\eqref{eq:fixed-upper-pullback} therefore give
\[
 \|T_{q_{\varepsilon,R}\chi Du\,\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}\|
 \leq C\|Du\|_\infty\left(
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\right).
\]
For the last term, multiplication by \(\chi\) only decreases the
positive annular majorants used in
\eqref{eq:uniform-error-operator}.  Hence
\[
 \|T_{q_{\varepsilon,R}(I-\chi Du)
 (\mathbf E_{x,\mathrm{near}}+\mathbf E_{\mathrm{far}})}\|
 \leq C(1+\|Du\|_\infty)
 \Lambda_{\psi,r_0}\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}.
\]
The norms in the last two displays are from
\(L^2(\widetilde\sigma)\) to \(L^2(\widetilde\omega)\).
It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:reverse-q-change}
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^q
 \leq C\left(
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
 +(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0})
   \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\right).
\end{equation}
The same estimates, with the same factor
\(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0}\), hold for the normalized \(q\)-testing
constants.
Expansion at \(y\) gives the reverse dual \(q\)-testing estimate.

These estimates use the target-radial cutoffs
\(q_{\varepsilon,R}\).  Since \(|\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)| \leq C|x-y|^{\alpha-n}\), the support comparison
\eqref{eq:target-source-cutoff-support} and
\cref{lem:annular-A2} also give
\begin{align*}
 &\sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \left\|\int
 (q_{\varepsilon,R}-s_{\varepsilon,R})(x,y)
 \mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)f(y)\,
d\widetilde\sigma(y)\right\|_{L^2(\widetilde\omega)}\leq C_L\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 \|f\|_{L^2(\widetilde\sigma)}.
\end{align*}
The same estimate holds for the adjoint and for both normalized testing
constants.  Combining it with \eqref{eq:reverse-q-change} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:reverse-source-change}
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^s
 \leq C\left(
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
 +(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0})
   \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\right),
\end{equation}
and the analogous forward and dual \(s\)-testing estimates, with the
same factor \(1+\Lambda_{\psi,r_0}\).  Equation
\eqref{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison} converts the left-hand sides to the
tangent-line constants.

Finally, under \(X=\Psi(x)\), \(Y=\Psi(y)\), the target-radial kernel \(\tau_{\varepsilon,R}(|X-Y|)\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(X,Y)\) pulls back to \(q_{\varepsilon,R}(x,y)\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}(x,y)\). The measures become \(\widetilde\sigma\) and
\(\widetilde\omega\), the source function becomes \(f\circ\Psi\), and
an original testing set \(Q\) becomes \(\Psi^{-1}Q\).  In particular, \(\|f\circ\Psi\|_{L^2(\widetilde\sigma)} =\|f\|_{L^2(\sigma)}\). Therefore
\begin{align*}
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}}^s(\sigma,\omega)
 &=\mathfrak N_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}}}^q
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega),\\
 \mathfrak T_{\mathbf K^{\alpha,n},\mathcal F}^s(\sigma,\omega)
 &=\mathfrak T_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}},\Psi^{-1}\mathcal F}^q
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega),\\
 \mathfrak T_{\mathbf K^{\alpha,n},\mathcal F}^{s,\mathrm{dual}}
   (\sigma,\omega)
 &=\mathfrak T_{\mathbf K^{\mathrm{pb}},\Psi^{-1}\mathcal F}^{q,\mathrm{dual}}
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega).
\end{align*}
Apply \eqref{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison} to the fractional Riesz
kernel in the original coordinates and to the conformal kernel in the
pullback coordinates.  Together with
\eqref{eq:one-direction-change} and
\eqref{eq:reverse-source-change}, these identities prove the norm and
testing comparisons in the proposition.

The small-distance error is summable by the Dini integral.  The

body_md:
\label{lem:admissible-families}
Each family occurring in the two lines of
\eqref{eq:strong-energy-definition} is admissible.  More precisely, this
holds for
\[
 \mathcal J=\bigcup_s
M_{r,\varepsilon\text{-deep}}(I_s),
 \qquad I=\dot\bigcup_s I_s,
\]
and for
\[
 \mathcal J=
M_{r,\varepsilon\text{-deep},\Omega\mathcal D}^{\ell}(I),
 \qquad I\in A\Omega\mathcal D,\quad \ell\geq0.
\]
The overlap constant is independent of the grid and of \(\ell\).

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:gamma-goodness}, \cite[(3.2) and (3.4)]{EnergyCommon}
gives the required inclusions and overlap estimates.  For the first
family, these estimates give
\[
 \gamma J\subset I_s,\qquad
 \sum_{J\in M_{r,\varepsilon\text{-deep}}(I_s)}
 \mathbf 1_{\gamma J}\leq\beta\mathbf 1_{I_s}.
\]
The \(I_s\) are disjoint, so summing in \(s\) gives
\eqref{eq:admissible-family}.  For an alternate top,
\cite[(3.4)]{EnergyCommon} gives
\[
 \gamma J\subset I,\qquad
 \sum_{J\in
M_{r,\varepsilon\text{-deep},\Omega\mathcal D}^{\ell}(I)}
 \mathbf 1_{\gamma J}\leq\beta\mathbf 1_I
\]
uniformly in the grid and in \(\ell\).

label: lem:C1-energy
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(p=n+1-\alpha\).  Direct differentiation gives
\begin{align*}
D_y\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(y,x)
 &=c_{\alpha,n}\left[
 -\frac{I}{|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|^p}
 +p\frac{(y-x)\otimes
D\Psi(y)^T(\Psi(y)-\Psi(x))}
 {|\Psi(y)-\Psi(x)|^{p+2}}\right].
\end{align*}
Here \(D_y\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(y,x)\) means the derivative of the map
\(y\mapsto\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(y,x)\).  By antisymmetry, it has the
opposite overall sign from \(D_y\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)\), where
\(y\) is the second kernel variable.
Thus \(|D_y\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(y,x)| \leq C|y-x|^{-p}\). If \(\omega(J)=0\), there is nothing to prove.  Otherwise put
\[
m_J^\omega=\frac1{\omega(J)}\int_Jy\,d\omega(y).
\]
Then \(m_J^\omega\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(J)\).  Hence, for
\(y\in J\) and \(\zeta\in[y,m_J^\omega]\), \(\zeta\in\overline{\operatorname{conv}}(J), \quad |\zeta-c_J| \leq\operatorname{diam} J \leq C_\Omega\ell(J)\). If \(x\notin\gamma J=\Omega(\gamma Q)\), then
\(\Omega^{-1}(x)\notin\gamma Q\), and therefore \(|x-c_J|\geq c_\Omega\gamma\ell(J)\). By the choice of \(\gamma\), these estimates give \(|\zeta-x|\approx_\Omega \ell(J)+|x-c_J|\). The fundamental theorem of
calculus and the mean-zero condition give
\begin{align*}
 \left|\left\langle
 \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu,\varphi_J
 \right\rangle_\omega\right|
 &\leq C\frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu)}{\ell(J)}
 \int_J|\varphi_J(y)|\,|y-m_J^\omega|\,d\omega(y)
 \leq C\frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu)}{\ell(J)}
 \|\varphi_J\|_{L^2(\omega)}
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_{L^2(\omega)}.
\end{align*}
No difference \(D\psi(s)-D\psi(t)\) is used.

label: lem:end-side-geometry
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:end-side-geometry}
There are \(A_0=A_0(n,\Omega)\) and
\(\gamma_0=\gamma_0(n,\Omega,A_0)\) such that, for
\(\gamma\geq\gamma_0\), the following holds whenever
\(J\cap L_0\neq\varnothing\).

If \(y\in\mathrm E(J^*)\), \(x,z\in J\cap L_0\), and \(u\) lies between
\(x^1-y^1\) and \(z^1-y^1\), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:end-geometry}
 |u|\approx\ell(J)+|y-c_J|,\qquad
 |y'|\leq\frac{CA_0}{\gamma}|u|,\qquad
 |x^1-z^1|\leq\frac C\gamma|u|.
\end{equation}
If \(y\in\mathrm S(J^*)\), then, with \(d(y)=|y'|\),
\begin{align}
d(y)&>0,\qquad
 \ell(J)\leq Cd(y),\qquad
 |y-c_J|\geq c\,d(y),
 \label{eq:side-geometry}\\
 \mathcal H^1(J^*\cap L_0)&\geq c\gamma\ell(J),\qquad
J^*\cap L_0\subset
 \{(t,0'):|t-y^1|\leq C\gamma d(y)\}.
 \label{eq:side-shadow}
\end{align}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\Lambda\) be a common biLipschitz constant for
\(\Omega,\Omega^{-1}\).  There are \(a,b>0\), depending only on
\(n,\Lambda\), such that \(J\subset B(c_J,b\ell(J)),\quad B(x_0,a(\gamma-1)\ell(J))\subset\gamma J \quad(x_0\in J)\). Choose \(A_0\geq8b/a\), and then
\(\gamma\geq\max\{2A_0,8b/a\}\).

Suppose \(y\in\mathrm E(J^*)\).  Since \(y\notin\gamma J\),
\(|y-c_J|\geq c\gamma\ell(J)\).  Put \(A=|y'-c_J'|,\quad B=|y^1-c_J^1|\). The end condition gives \(A\leq A_0B/\gamma\), and hence
\(B\approx|y-c_J|\).  Points of \(J\cap L_0\) have first coordinate within
\(b\ell(J)\) of \(c_J^1\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:end-geometry}.

Now let \(y\in\mathrm S(J^*)\), and fix \(x_0\in J\cap L_0\).  The side
condition gives \(B<\frac{\gamma}{A_0}A \leq\frac{\gamma}{A_0}\{d(y)+b\ell(J)\}\). Since \(y\notin\gamma J\), \(a(\gamma-1)\ell(J) \leq|y-x_0|\leq B+b\ell(J)+d(y)\). Our choices allow the terms containing \(\ell(J)\) on the right to be
absorbed on the left.  Thus \(d(y)\geq cA_0\ell(J)\), and
\(|y-c_J|\geq c\,d(y)\).  We also obtain
\(|y^1-x_0^1|\leq C\gamma d(y)\).  Intersecting
\(B(x_0,a(\gamma-1)\ell(J))\) with \(L_0\) gives the lower bound for
\(\mathcal H^1(J^*\cap L_0)\).  Finally,
\(\operatorname{diam} J^*\leq C\gamma\ell(J)\leq C\gamma d(y)\), which gives
\eqref{eq:side-shadow}.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Terms with \(\omega(J)=0\) vanish.  Since \(\omega\) is supported on
\(L_0\), the variance of \(\mathbf x\) on \(J\) is the variance of the
first coordinate.  Put
\[
a_J=\frac{P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm E(J^*)}\sigma)}
 {\ell(J)},\qquad
b_J=\frac{P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)}
 {\ell(J)}.
\]
Since \(I\setminus J^*=\mathrm E(J^*)\dot\cup\mathrm S(J^*)\),
linearity of \(P^\alpha\) and \((a_J+b_J)^2\leq2a_J^2+2b_J^2\)
reduce the proof to the two corresponding energy sums.
By \cref{lem:end-reversal} and the variance identity,
\[
a_J^2\|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2
 \leq C\int_J
 \left|R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}
  (\mathbf 1_{\mathrm E(J^*)}\sigma)
 -\mathbb E_J^\omega R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}
 (\mathbf 1_{\mathrm E(J^*)}\sigma)\right|^2d\omega.
\]
First take a finite subfamily
\(\mathcal J_0\subset\mathcal J\).  Terms for which
\(I\setminus J^*=\varnothing\) have zero Poisson factor and may be
discarded.  If no term remains, there is nothing to prove.  Otherwise
put
\[
d_0=\min_{J\in\mathcal J_0}\operatorname{dist}(J,I\setminus J^*),
 \qquad
D_0=\max_{J\in\mathcal J_0}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in J\\y\in I\setminus J^*}}|x-y|.
\]
Since \(J^*=\gamma J\), quasicube geometry gives \(d_0\geq c_\Omega(\gamma-1) \min_{J\in\mathcal J_0}\ell(J)>0, \quad D_0\leq\operatorname{diam} I\). Choose one tangent-line truncation with \(0<\delta<d_0,\quad R>D_0\). Then \(t_{\delta,R}=1\) on
\(J\times(I\setminus J^*)\) for every \(J\in\mathcal J_0\).
The half-open convention gives the partition \(I=J^*\dot\cup\mathrm E(J^*)\dot\cup\mathrm S(J^*)\). Consequently, for \(x\in J\),
\begin{align*}
 \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}
   (\mathbf 1_{\mathrm E(J^*)}\sigma)(x)
 &=
 \mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_I\sigma)(x)
 -\mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_{J^*}\sigma)(x)
 -\mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)(x).
\end{align*}
In the next three testing estimates,
each transform denotes this fixed tangent-line truncation.
After subtracting the \(\omega\)-average on \(J\), the triangle
inequality gives three oscillation terms.  Testing on \(I\) gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal J_0}\int_J
 |R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_I\sigma)|^2\,d\omega
 &\leq\beta\int_I
 |R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_I\sigma)|^2\,d\omega
 \leq\beta\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^2\sigma(I).
\end{align*}
Testing on each \(J^*\), followed by
\eqref{eq:admissible-family}, gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal J_0}\int_J
 |R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_{J^*}\sigma)|^2\,d\omega
 &\leq\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^2
       \sum_{J\in\mathcal J_0}\sigma(J^*)
 \leq\beta\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^2\sigma(I).
\end{align*}
For the side term, apply \cref{lem:C1-energy} to a vector test
function whose only nonzero component is the first one.  By duality,
\[
 \int_J\left|R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}
 (\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)
 -\mathbb E_J^\omega R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}
 (\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)\right|^2d\omega
 \leq Cb_J^2\|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2.
\]
All bounds are uniform in the truncation.  Letting the finite
subfamilies \(\mathcal J_0\) increase to \(\mathcal J\), monotone
convergence applies to the nonnegative energy sums.  It remains to
estimate
\[
B=\sum_{J\in\mathcal J}
 \left(
 \frac{P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)}
 {\ell(J)}\right)^2
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2.
\]
Write
\[
 \mathcal P^\alpha(J,\nu)
 \approx_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^n}
 \left(\frac{\ell(J)}
 {(\ell(J)+|y-c_J|)^2}\right)^{n-\alpha}d\nu(y).
\]
Suppose first that \(n-1\leq\alpha<n\).  Since
\(\mathrm S(J^*)\subset J^c\), \(P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma) \leq C\mathcal P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)\). Using
\(\|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2\leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J)\) and the
one-tailed condition gives
\begin{align*}
 &\left(
 \frac{P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)}
 {\ell(J)}\right)^2
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2\leq C\mathcal A_2^\alpha
 \int_{\mathrm S(J^*)}
 \left(\frac{\ell(J)}
 {\ell(J)+|y-c_J|}\right)^{n+1-\alpha}d\sigma(y).
\end{align*}
If \(0\leq\alpha<n-1\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\begin{align*}
P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)^2
 &\leq C_\Omega
 \mathcal P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)
 \int_{\mathrm S(J^*)}
 \frac{\ell(J)^{\alpha+2-n}}
 {(\ell(J)+|y-c_J|)^2}\,d\sigma(y).
\end{align*}
Using
\(\|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2\leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J)\) and \(\omega(J)\mathcal P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma) \leq C\mathcal A_2^\alpha\ell(J)^{n-\alpha}\), we obtain
\begin{align*}
 &\left(
 \frac{P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{\mathrm S(J^*)}\sigma)}
 {\ell(J)}\right)^2
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2\leq C\mathcal A_2^\alpha
 \int_{\mathrm S(J^*)}
 \left(\frac{\ell(J)}
 {\ell(J)+|y-c_J|}\right)^2d\sigma(y).
\end{align*}
Thus, with \(q_\alpha=\min\{2,n+1-\alpha\}>1\),
\begin{equation*}
B\leq C\mathcal A_2^\alpha
 \int_I\sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal J\\y\in\mathrm S(J^*)}}
 \left(\frac{\ell(J)}
 {\ell(J)+|y-c_J|}\right)^{q_\alpha}d\sigma(y).
\end{equation*}
By \cref{lem:end-side-geometry}, if \(d(y)=\operatorname{dist}(y,L_0)\) and
\(y\in\mathrm S(J^*)\), then \eqref{eq:side-geometry} and
\eqref{eq:side-shadow} hold.
Hence, by bounded overlap,
\[
 \sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal J\\y\in\mathrm S(J^*)}}\ell(J)
 \leq\frac C\gamma
 \int_{|t-y^1|\leq C\gamma d(y)}
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal J}\mathbf 1_{J^*}(t,0)\,dt
 \leq C\beta d(y).
\]
Moreover, \eqref{eq:side-geometry} gives
\(\ell(J)\leq Cd(y)\) and
\(|y-c_J|\geq c\,d(y)\).  Since \(1<q_\alpha\leq2\),
the number \(t_J=\ell(J)/d(y)\) satisfies \(t_J\leq C\), and hence
\(t_J^{q_\alpha}\leq C^{q_\alpha-1}t_J\).  Therefore
\begin{align*}
 &\sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal J\\y\in\mathrm S(J^*)}}
 \left(\frac{\ell(J)}
 {\ell(J)+|y-c_J|}\right)^{q_\alpha}\leq
C\sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal J\\y\in\mathrm S(J^*)}}
 \left(\frac{\ell(J)}{d(y)}\right)^{q_\alpha}
 \leq
 \frac C{d(y)}
 \sum_{\substack{J\in\mathcal J\\y\in\mathrm S(J^*)}}\ell(J)
 \leq C\beta.
\end{align*}
Thus
\(B\leq C\beta\mathcal A_2^\alpha\sigma(I)\), which proves
\eqref{eq:forward-hole}.

label: lem:fill-hole
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\mathfrak P\) be the set of common point masses, and write
\[
 \omega(Q,\mathfrak P)
 =\omega(Q)-\sup_{p\in Q\cap\mathfrak P}\omega(\{p\}),
\]
where the supremum of the empty set is \(0\).  If
\(J^*\cap\mathfrak P\neq\varnothing\), choose a largest common
\(\omega\)-atom \(p_J\).  Such an atom exists because
\(\omega(J^*)<\infty\): if the positive supremum of the common atomic
masses were not attained, infinitely many of them would exceed half of
that supremum.
If \(p_J\in J\), the minimizing property of variance gives
\[
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2
 \leq\int_J|x-p_J|^2\,d\omega(x)
 \leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P).
\]
If \(p_J\notin J\), then
the half-open sets \(J\) and \(\{p_J\}\) are disjoint.  Since \(p_J\)
is a largest common \(\omega\)-atom in \(J^*\), \(\omega(J) \leq \omega\bigl(J^*\setminus\{p_J\}\bigr) =\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P)\). The minimizing property of the barycenter, followed by the quasicube
diameter bound, now gives
\begin{align*}
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2
 &\leq\int_J|x-c_J|^2\,d\omega(x)\leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J)
 \leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P).
\end{align*}
When \(J^*\cap\mathfrak P\) is empty,
\(\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P)=\omega(J^*)\).  Centering at \(c_J\) gives
\[
 \|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2
 \leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J)
 \leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J^*)
 =C\ell(J)^2\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P).
\]
Hence \(\|P_J^\omega\mathbf x\|_2^2 \leq C\ell(J)^2\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P)\). Also, \(P^\alpha(J,\mathbf 1_{J^*}\sigma) \leq C\frac{\sigma(\gamma J)}{\ell(J)^{n-\alpha}}\). Thus the left side of \eqref{eq:fill-hole} is at most
\[
C\sum_{J\in\mathcal J}
 \frac{\sigma(J^*)^2\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P)}
 {\ell(J)^{2(n-\alpha)}}.
\]
Since the puncture is in the \(\omega\)-factor, we use the starred
punctured condition.  Since
\(\ell(J^*)=\gamma\ell(J)\), it gives
\[
 \frac{\sigma(J^*)\omega(J^*,\mathfrak P)}
 {\ell(J)^{2(n-\alpha)}}
 \leq C_\gamma A_2^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}.
\]
Bounded overlap now gives
\[
C_\gamma A_2^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal J}\sigma(J^*)
 \leq C_\gamma\beta
A_2^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}\sigma(I).
\]
Interchanging \(\sigma\) and \(\omega\) punctures the
\(\sigma\)-factor.  This gives the unstarred constant in the dual
estimate stated above.

Write \(J=\Omega Q\).  The biLipschitz bounds imply \(\operatorname{diam} J\leq C_\Omega\ell(J),\quad \operatorname{dist}(J,(\gamma J)^c)\geq c_\Omega(\gamma-1)\ell(J)\), where the second inequality remains valid for half-open quasicubes after
decreasing \(c_\Omega\).  If \(3J\cap L_0=\varnothing\), then
\(L_0\subset(3J)^c\).  The preceding distance bound with \(\gamma=3\)
therefore gives \(\operatorname{dist}(J,L_0)\geq c_\Omega\ell(J)\).  This proves the
first assertion.

For the second, choose \(\zeta\in3J\cap L_0\).  Since
\(w_t\in\operatorname{conv}(J)\), we have
\(|w_t-c_J|\leq C_\Omega\ell(J)\), and hence
\(|w_t-\zeta|\leq C_\Omega\ell(J)\).  This gives the first bound.
Since \(x\notin\gamma J\),
\(|x-c_J|\geq c_\Omega\gamma\ell(J)\).  Therefore, after increasing
\(\gamma\), \(|x-w_t|\geq |x-c_J|-|w_t-c_J| \geq c_\Omega\gamma\ell(J)\). Subtracting the transverse bound gives the second and third bounds.
The estimates for \(|x-c_J|\) and \(|w_t-c_J|\) give the last
comparison.

title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:backward-choice-one
title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(p=n+1-\alpha\), \(q=p-1=n-\alpha\), and write \(h=y-z=(h_1,h'),\quad w_t=z+th\). For \(x=(x^1,0)\in L_0\setminus\gamma J\), set \(a=w_t^1-x^1,\quad u=w_t',\quad b=u+\psi(w_t^1)-\psi(x^1),\quad r=(a^2+|b|^2)^{1/2}\). BiLipschitz quasicube geometry gives \(|u|\leq\eta|a|,\quad |b|\leq\delta|a|,\quad r\approx|a|\approx\ell(J)+|x-c_J|\), where \(\eta=\frac{C_\Omega}{\gamma}, \quad \delta=\eta+\|D\psi\|_\infty\). The bound in \eqref{eq:graph-map}, followed by the choice of \(\gamma\)
above, ensures that
\begin{align}
 \delta^2+p\delta(1+\|D\psi\|_\infty)&\leq q/2,
 \label{eq:backward-choice-one}\\
p\eta\{1+\delta(1+\|D\psi\|_\infty)\}&\leq1/2.\notag
\end{align}

Suppose first that \(|h'|\leq|h_1|\).  If \(h_1=0\), then \(y=z\),
so the desired estimate is trivial.  We may therefore assume
\(h_1\neq0\).  For \(\phi_x(t)=a r^{-p}\), direct differentiation gives
\begin{align*}
 \phi_x'(t)
 &=\frac{h_1}{r^{p+2}}N_1(t,x),\\
N_1(t,x)
 &=-qa^2+|b|^2
 -pa\,b\cdot\frac{h'}{h_1}
 -pa\,b\cdot D\psi(w_t^1).
\end{align*}
By \eqref{eq:backward-choice-one}, \(N_1(t,x)\leq-\frac q2a^2\). The sign is fixed for every \(x,t\).  Integration first in \(t\), then
in \(x\), yields
\[
 \left|
 (R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}\nu)(y)
 -(R_{\Psi,1}^{\alpha,n}\nu)(z)
 \right|
 \geq c|h_1|\int\!\!\int_0^1\frac{a^2}{r^{p+2}}\,dt\,d\nu(x)
 \geq c|h_1|\frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu)}{\ell(J)}.
\]

Suppose next that \(|h'|>|h_1|\).  Differentiate the transverse vector:
\begin{align}
 \frac d{dt}(u r^{-p})
 &=h'r^{-p}+\mathbf e_x(t),\notag\\
 \mathbf e_x(t)
 &=-p\,u r^{-p-2}
 \left\{ah_1+b\cdot h'
 +b\cdot D\psi(w_t^1)h_1\right\},\notag\\
 |\mathbf e_x(t)|
 &\leq p\eta\{1+\delta(1+\|D\psi\|_\infty)\}
 |h'|r^{-p}
 \leq\frac12|h'|r^{-p}.
 \label{eq:backward-case-two}
\end{align}
The reverse triangle inequality gives
\begin{align*}
 \left|\int_{L_0}\int_0^1
 \bigl(h'r^{-p}+\mathbf e_x(t)\bigr)\,dt\,d\nu(x)\right|
 &\geq |h'|\int_{L_0}\int_0^1r^{-p}\,dt\,d\nu(x)
 -\int_{L_0}\int_0^1|\mathbf e_x(t)|\,dt\,d\nu(x)\\
 &\geq\frac{|h'|}{2}
 \int_{L_0}\int_0^1r^{-p}\,dt\,d\nu(x).
\end{align*}
Consequently,
\[
 \left|
 (\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu(y))'
 -(\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu(z))'
 \right|
 \geq c|h'|\frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu)}{\ell(J)}
 \geq c|h_1|\frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu)}{\ell(J)}.
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:backward-reversal}.  The calculation uses
\(|\psi(s)-\psi(t)|\leq\|D\psi\|_\infty|s-t|\) and the pointwise
bound for \(D\psi\), but no modulus of \(D\psi\).

\(P^\alpha(J,\nu)/\ell(J)\).

label: lem:backward-hole
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a finite subfamily \(\mathcal J_0\subset\mathcal J\).  Terms for
which \(I\setminus\gamma J=\varnothing\) have zero Poisson factor and
may be discarded.  If no term remains, there is nothing to prove.
Otherwise put
\[
d_0=\min_{J\in\mathcal J_0}
 \operatorname{dist}(J,I\setminus\gamma J),
 \qquad
D_0=\max_{J\in\mathcal J_0}
 \sup_{\substack{x\in J\\y\in I\setminus\gamma J}}|x-y|.
\]
Quasicube geometry gives \(d_0\geq c_\Omega(\gamma-1) \min_{J\in\mathcal J_0}\ell(J)>0, \quad D_0\leq\operatorname{diam} I\). Choose \(0<\delta<d_0,\quad R>D_0\). Then \(t_{\delta,R}=1\) on every
\(J\times(I\setminus\gamma J)\), \(J\in\mathcal J_0\).  In the sums
below, \(J\) ranges over \(\mathcal J_0\).  The estimates are uniform
in \(\mathcal J_0,\delta\), and \(R\).
Let \(\mathcal J_{\rm off}=\{J\in\mathcal J_0:3J\cap L_0=\varnothing\}\). For \(J\in\mathcal J_{\rm off}\), put \(\nu_J=\mathbf 1_{I\setminus\gamma J}\omega\). The first part of \cref{lem:weak-backward} and
\(\|P_J^\sigma\mathbf x\|_2^2\leq C\ell(J)^2\sigma(J)\) give
\begin{align*}
 &\left(
 \frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu_J)}{\ell(J)}\right)^2
 \|P_J^\sigma\mathbf x\|_2^2
 \leq C\int_J|\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J|^2\,d\sigma.
\end{align*}
For \(x\in J\), the common truncation gives the pointwise identity
\[
 \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J(x)
 =
 \mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_I\omega)(x)
 -
 \mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_{\gamma J}\omega)(x).
\]
The testing transforms below use this fixed
tangent-line truncation.
Since \(J\subset\gamma J\) and
\(\sum_J\mathbf 1_{\gamma J}\leq\beta\mathbf 1_I\), summation gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{J\in\mathcal J_{\rm off}}
 \int_J|\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J|^2\,d\sigma
 &\leq2\beta\int_I
 |\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_I\omega)|^2\,d\sigma+2\sum_{J\in\mathcal J_{\rm off}}\int_{\gamma J}
 |\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_{\gamma J}\omega)|^2\,d\sigma
 \leq C\beta
 \bigl(\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\bigr)^2
 \omega(I).
\end{align*}
Here the last line uses dual testing on \(I\) and on every \(\gamma J\),
together with
\(\sum_{J\in\mathcal J_{\rm off}}\omega(\gamma J)
\leq\beta\omega(I)\).

For \(3J\cap L_0\neq\varnothing\), put \(\nu_J=\mathbf 1_{I\setminus\gamma J}\omega, \quad a_J=\frac{P^\alpha(J,\nu_J)}{\ell(J)}\). If \(\sigma(J)=0\), the corresponding energy term is zero.  Suppose
that \(\sigma(J)>0\).  For the first coordinate, the variance identity
and \cref{lem:backward-reversal} give
\begin{align*}
a_J^2\int_J
   |y^1-(m_J^\sigma)^1|^2\,d\sigma(y)
 &=
 \frac{a_J^2}{2\sigma(J)}
 \int_J\int_J|y^1-z^1|^2\,d\sigma(y)\,d\sigma(z)\\
 &\leq
 \frac C{2\sigma(J)}
 \int_J\int_J
 |\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J(y)
  -\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J(z)|^2
 \,d\sigma(y)\,d\sigma(z)\\
 &=
C\int_J
 |\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J
  -\mathbb E_J^\sigma
   \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J|^2\,d\sigma\\
 &\leq
C\int_J|\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J|^2\,d\sigma.
\end{align*}
For \(2\leq k\leq n\), the minimizing property of the mean and the
second part of \cref{lem:weak-backward} give
\begin{align*}
a_J^2\int_J|y^k-(m_J^\sigma)^k|^2\,d\sigma(y)
 &\leq a_J^2\int_J|y^k|^2\,d\sigma(y)
 \leq C\int_J
 |R_{\Psi,k}^{\alpha,n}\nu_J(y)|^2\,d\sigma(y).
\end{align*}
Adding the coordinate estimates gives
\[
a_J^2\|P_J^\sigma\mathbf x\|_2^2
 \leq C\int_J|\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J|^2\,d\sigma.
\]
The same pointwise identity gives
\[
 \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}\nu_J(x)
 =
 \mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_I\omega)(x)
 -
 \mathbf R_{\Psi,\delta,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}
   (\mathbf 1_{\gamma J}\omega)(x),
 \qquad x\in J.
\]
The first term is summed using bounded overlap and dual testing on \(I\).
For the second, use dual testing on \(\gamma J\) and
\[
 \sum_J\omega(\gamma J)\leq\beta\omega(I).
\]
The estimates are uniform in \(\mathcal J_0\) and in the common
truncation.  Letting \(\mathcal J_0\) increase to \(\mathcal J\) and
using monotone convergence for the nonnegative energy sums gives
\eqref{eq:backward-hole}.

label: prop:C1-energy-reversal
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:C1-energy-reversal}
Let \(\psi\in C^1(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^{n-1})\) satisfy
\eqref{eq:graph-map}.  Let \(\omega\) be supported on \(L_0\).  For every
globally biLipschitz quasicube map \(\Omega\),
\begin{align}
 \mathcal E_{\alpha,\Omega}^{\mathrm{strong}}(\sigma,\omega)
 &\leq C\left(
 \mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n},\Omega}
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha}\right),
 \label{eq:forward-strong-line}\\
 \mathcal E_{\alpha,\Omega}^{\mathrm{strong,dual}}(\sigma,\omega)
 &\leq C\left(
 \mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n},\Omega}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha}\right).
 \label{eq:backward-strong-line}
\end{align}
Up to constants depending on the fixed quasicube map, the two quantities
on the left are the strong energy constants in
\cite[Definition~5]{EnergyCommon}, since
\(|J|^{1/n}\approx_\Omega\ell(J)\).  The estimates include both lines of
\eqref{eq:strong-energy-definition}, and are uniform in the quasigrid and
in the refinement index \(\ell\).  No modulus of \(D\psi\) occurs.

title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(\zeta(t)=\Omega^{-1}(te_1)\).  Every coordinate
\(\zeta_k\) is strictly increasing.  If
\(C=\prod_k[d_k,d_k+\ell)\), then
\[
 \{t:\zeta(t)\in C\}
 =\bigcap_k\{t:d_k\leq\zeta_k(t)<d_k+\ell\},
\]
an intersection of half-open intervals.  This proves the first part.

For the second, put \(h=b-a\), \(\ell=8C_nh\), and define
\[
C_S=\prod_{k=1}^n[d_k,d_k+\ell)
\]
by
\[
d_1=\zeta_1(a),\qquad
d_2=\zeta_2(b)-\ell,\qquad
d_k=\frac{\zeta_k(a)+\zeta_k(b)-\ell}{2}
 \quad(3\leq k\leq n).
\]
For \(a\leq t<b\),
\[
 0\leq\zeta_1(t)-d_1\leq C_nh<\ell,
 \qquad
 0<d_2+\ell-\zeta_2(t)\leq\ell,
\]
and \(\zeta_2(t)>d_2\).  For \(3\leq k\leq n\), \(\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\zeta_k([a,b]), \{d_k,d_k+\ell\}\bigr) \geq\frac{\ell-C_nh}{2} \geq\frac{7\ell}{16}\). Thus the path \(\zeta([a,b])\) meets only the first lower face at
\(\zeta(a)\) and the second upper face at \(\zeta(b)\).
Moreover, \(t<a\) is excluded by the first coordinate, while
\(t\geq b\) is excluded by the second coordinate.  Hence
\(\zeta(t)\in C_S\) exactly when \(a\leq t<b\).  Take
\(Q_S=\Omega C_S\).
The derivative bounds and the biLipschitz bounds for \(\Omega\) give
\eqref{eq:auxiliary-size}.

label: lem:nested-arcs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nested-arcs}
Let \(\Gamma\) be a compact regular \(C^1\) curve.  Assume that it is
simple: the parametrization is one-to-one on the interval for an open
curve and on the parameter circle for a closed curve.  There is
a finite family of graph charts and global graph extensions with the
following property.  For every \(A>1\), there is a finite disjoint Borel
decomposition
\[
 \Gamma=\dot\bigcup_{i=1}^N\Gamma_i
\]
and nested graph arcs \(\Gamma_i\Subset\widehat{\Gamma}_i \Subset\Gamma_i^*\) with the following properties.  Let \(\mathcal U_i\) be the rigid motion
for the \(i\)-th arc.  In every formula concerning this fixed chart, we
relabel the rigid images
\(\mathcal U_i\Gamma\),
\(\mathcal U_i\Gamma_i\),
\(\mathcal U_i\widehat{\Gamma}_i\), and
\(\mathcal U_i\Gamma_i^*\) as
\(\Gamma\), \(\Gamma_i\),
\(\widehat{\Gamma}_i\), and \(\Gamma_i^*\), respectively.
In these rigid coordinates, one of the graph maps in the fixed family has
the form \(\Psi_i(x_1,x')=(x_1,x'+\psi_i(x_1))\) and a half-open interval \(I_i\subset L_0\) such that \(\Psi_i^{-1}(\Gamma_i)\subset I_i\). Except for the last arc of an open curve, equality holds.  For that last
arc, \(I_i\) includes an additional terminal segment on which every
pulled-back measure supported on \(\Gamma\) has zero mass.

If \(\widetilde{\Gamma}^{(i)}=\Psi_i^{-1}(\Gamma)\) then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:tube-localization}
 \{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,I_i)\leq A|I_i|\}
 \cap\widetilde{\Gamma}^{(i)}
 \subset\Psi_i^{-1}(\widehat{\Gamma}_i)\subset L_0.
\end{equation}
The fixed graph slopes can be made smaller than any prescribed positive
constant.  In the \(C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\) case, the fixed maps can be
chosen as in \cref{lem:graph-extension}.  Thus their biLipschitz
constants and the constants in \cref{lem:axis-sections} are fixed before
\(A\).  Only the final subdivision into the arcs \(\Gamma_i\) depends
on \(A\).

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(M=[a,b]\) for an open curve.  For a closed curve, let \(M=\mathbb R/(b-a)\mathbb Z\) and regard \(\Phi\) as a one-to-one embedding of the parameter circle
\(M\).  We use the parameter distance on \(M\).

For every \(t_0\in M\), choose a rigid motion \(\mathcal U_{t_0}\) that
sends \(\Phi(t_0)\) to the origin and \(\Phi'(t_0)\) to \(e_1\).  After
shrinking the parameter
neighborhood, write \(\mathcal U_{t_0}\Phi(t) =\bigl(u_{t_0}(t),g_{t_0}(u_{t_0}(t))\bigr)\). The neighborhoods can be chosen so that, with one constant \(c_0>0\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:parameter-coordinate-comparison}
c_0\leq u_{t_0}'(t)\leq1.
\end{equation}
The slopes of the functions \(g_{t_0}\) can be made as small as desired.
For two parameters \(s,t\) in the same neighborhood,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:parameter-coordinate-distance}
c_0d_M(s,t)
 \leq |u_{t_0}(s)-u_{t_0}(t)|
 \leq d_M(s,t).
\end{equation}

Choose finitely many triples \(V_\nu\Subset\widehat V_\nu\Subset V_\nu^*, \quad 1\leq\nu\leq N_0\), such that the \(V_\nu\) cover \(M\) and every \(V_\nu^*\) lies in one
of the graph neighborhoods above.  The intervals may be chosen with a
fixed relative collar.  By
\eqref{eq:parameter-coordinate-comparison}, the corresponding
\(u_\nu\)-intervals have a fixed relative collar as well.  Our choice of
rigid motion gives \(g_\nu(0)=0\), after relabeling the graph coordinate
so that \(u_\nu(t_0)=0\).  At an endpoint of an open curve, extend the
local graph by its tangent affine function to a slightly larger
\(u_\nu\)-interval.  This is a \(C^1\) extension.  If the original
derivative has a Dini modulus, then the derivative of this one-sided
extension has the same Dini integral, up to an absolute constant.

Extend every \(g_\nu\) by \cref{lem:graph-extension}, and denote the
resulting graph shear by \(\Psi_\nu\).  Put \(K=\max_{1\leq\nu\leq N_0} \max\{\operatorname{Lip}(\Psi_\nu),\operatorname{Lip}(\Psi_\nu^{-1})\}\). For each \(\nu\), let \(R_\nu\) be the diagonal rotation used in
\eqref{eq:coordinate-monotonicity}, and put \(\Omega_\nu=\Psi_\nu^{-1}\circ R_\nu\). The rotations are isometries.  Hence the biLipschitz constants of the
finitely many maps \(\Omega_\nu\) are bounded in terms of \(K\).  Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:axis-family-constant}
C_{\rm ax}=\max_{1\leq\nu\leq N_0}C_{\Omega_\nu},
\end{equation}
where \(C_{\Omega_\nu}\) is the constant in
\eqref{eq:auxiliary-size}.  Thus \(K\) and \(C_{\rm ax}\) have been fixed
without using \(A\).

The rigid motions preserve distance.  Simplicity and compactness give \(d_\nu:=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\Phi(\overline V_\nu), \Phi(M\setminus\widehat V_\nu)\bigr)>0\). Thus \(d_0:=\min_{1\leq\nu\leq N_0}d_\nu>0\).
Let \(\lambda>0\) be a Lebesgue number for the cover
\(\{V_\nu\}_{\nu=1}^{N_0}\).  The numbers \(d_0\) and \(\lambda\) also
depend only on the finite chart family.  Fix the prescribed number
\(A>1\), and choose \(0<h<\min\left\{\lambda,\frac{d_0}{4AK}\right\}\). Partition \(M\) into consecutive arcs \(J_i\) of parameter length at
most \(h\).  In the closed case these are cyclic half-open arcs.  In the
open case use half-open arcs, except that the last arc contains \(b\).
For each \(J_i\), choose \(\nu(i)\) such that
\(\overline J_i\subset V_{\nu(i)}\), and put
\[
 \Gamma_i=\Phi(J_i),\qquad
 \widehat{\Gamma}_i=\Phi(\widehat V_{\nu(i)}),\qquad
 \Gamma_i^*=\Phi(V_{\nu(i)}^*).
\]
Work in the rigid coordinates \(\mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\), and write
\(\Psi_i=\Psi_{\nu(i)}\).

If \(J_i\) is not the last arc of an open curve, define \(I_i=u_{\nu(i)}(J_i)e_1\). For the last open arc \(J_i=[t_{N-1},b]\), put
\(\beta_i=u_{\nu(i)}(b)\), choose \(0<\delta_i\leq \min\left\{h,\frac{d_0}{4K}\right\}\), and set \(I_i=[u_{\nu(i)}(t_{N-1}),\beta_i+\delta_i)e_1\). The added terminal segment is \(G_i=(\beta_i,\beta_i+\delta_i)e_1\).  No point of the local curve has first coordinate
larger than \(\beta_i\).  Every point of the remaining curve is at least
\(d_0\) from
\(\mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\Phi(\overline V_{\nu(i)})\), while every point of
\(\Psi_i(G_i)\) is within \(K\delta_i\) of
\(\mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\Phi(b)\).  Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ghost-zero}
 \Psi_i(G_i)\cap\mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\Gamma=\varnothing.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\bigl(\Psi_i(G_i),
 \mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\Phi(M\setminus\widehat V_{\nu(i)})\bigr)
 \geq d_0-K\delta_i\geq\frac{d_0}{2}.
\]

For every \(i\), including the last open arc, we therefore have \(\operatorname{dist}\left(\Psi_i(I_i), \mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\Phi(M\setminus\widehat V_{\nu(i)})\right) \geq\frac{d_0}{2}\). Equation \eqref{eq:parameter-coordinate-distance} and the definition of
\(G_i\) give \(|I_i|\leq2h\).
Let \(x\in\widetilde{\Gamma}^{(i)} \setminus\Psi_i^{-1}(\widehat{\Gamma}_i)\). There is \(t\in M\setminus\widehat V_{\nu(i)}\) such that
\(\Psi_i(x)=\mathcal U_{\nu(i)}\Phi(t)\).  Hence
\begin{align*}
 \operatorname{dist}(x,I_i)
 &\geq K^{-1}
 \operatorname{dist}\bigl(\Psi_i(x),\Psi_i(I_i)\bigr)\geq\frac{d_0}{2K}
 >2Ah
 \geq A|I_i|.
\end{align*}
This proves the first inclusion in
\eqref{eq:tube-localization}.  On \(\widehat V_{\nu(i)}\), the extended
graph agrees with the original graph.  Therefore \(\Psi_i^{-1}(\widehat{\Gamma}_i) =u_{\nu(i)}(\widehat V_{\nu(i)})e_1\subset L_0\).
For a closed curve, each partition point belongs to the cyclic interval
that starts there and not to the interval that ends there.  For an open
curve, the first endpoint belongs to the first interval and the last
endpoint belongs to the last interval.  Equation \eqref{eq:ghost-zero}
shows that \(G_i\) is disjoint from the pulled-back support.

For each arc \(J_i\) in the final partition, set
\(R_i=R_{\nu(i)}\) and
\(\Omega_i=\Omega_{\nu(i)}=\Psi_i^{-1}\circ R_i\).  If the
prescribed number satisfies \(A>2C_{\rm ax}\), then the auxiliary quasicubes lie in the tube in
\eqref{eq:tube-localization}.  Indeed, if \(S\subset I_i\) and
\(P_S=Q_S\) is the quasicube from \cref{lem:axis-sections}, then
\begin{align*}
 3P_S
 &\subset\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq C_{\Omega_i}|S|\}\\
 &\subset\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,I_i)\leq C_{\rm ax}|I_i|\}
 \subset\{x:\operatorname{dist}(x,I_i)\leq A|I_i|\}.
\end{align*}
Consequently, \(3P_S\cap\widetilde{\Gamma}^{(i)} \subset\Psi_i^{-1}(\widehat{\Gamma}_i)\subset L_0\). This is the form used in \cref{prop:localized-testing}.

label: lem:Hardy
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Hardy}
Let \(\lambda,\tau\) be locally finite positive Borel measures on
\([0,\infty)\), and let
\(s>0\).  Assume
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Hardy-no-common-zero}
 \lambda(\{0\})\tau(\{0\})=0.
\end{equation}
At \(r=0\), if \(\tau(\{0\})>0\), interpret
\(r^{-s}\lambda([0,r])\) as zero and replace \([r,\infty)\) by
\((0,\infty)\) in the second integrand.  Then
\begin{align*}
 \int_0^\infty
 [r^{-s}\lambda([0,r])]^2\,d\tau(r)
 &\leq4B_1\lambda([0,\infty)),\\
 \int_0^\infty
 \left[\int_{[r,\infty)}t^{-s}\,d\lambda(t)\right]^2d\tau(r)
 &\leq4B_2\lambda([0,\infty)),
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
B_1&=\sup_{\rho>0}\lambda([0,\rho])
 \int_{[\rho,\infty)}r^{-2s}\,d\tau(r), \ \
B_2=\sup_{\rho>0}\tau([0,\rho])
 \int_{[\rho,\infty)}t^{-2s}\,d\lambda(t).
\end{align*}

label: eq:Stieltjes-increasing
title: Proof
body_md:
These are the \(p=2\) direct and dual two-weight Hardy inequalities for
positive Borel measures; see \cite{Hardy}.  We include the
Stieltjes-measure proof.  Consider
\[
Hf(r)=r^{-s}\int_{[0,r]}f(t)\,d\lambda(t).
\]
Put \(F(r)=\lambda([0,r]),\quad d\nu(r)=r^{-2s}d\tau(r),\quad G(r)=\nu([r,\infty))\). Here \(\nu\) is defined on \((0,\infty)\); a possible atom at zero is
treated at the end of the proof.
Thus \(F(r)G(r)\leq B_1\).  The elementary Stieltjes estimates
\begin{align}
 \int_{[0,r]}F(t)^{-1/2}\,d\lambda(t)
 &\leq2F(r)^{1/2},
 \label{eq:Stieltjes-increasing}\\
 \int_{[t,\infty)}G(r)^{-1/2}\,d\nu(r)
 &\leq2G(t)^{1/2}
 \label{eq:Stieltjes-decreasing}
\end{align}
follow from the distribution functions.  Indeed, for $0<A=F(r)<\infty$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_{[0,r]}F(t)^{-1/2}\,d\lambda(t)
 &=A^{1/2}+\frac12\int_0^A u^{-3/2}
   \lambda\{t\in[0,r]:0<F(t)\leq u\}\,du\\
 &\leq A^{1/2}+\frac12\int_0^A u^{-1/2}\,du=2A^{1/2}.
 \end{split}
\]
Here $\lambda\{t\in[0,r]:0<F(t)\leq u\}\leq u$.
For the second estimate, use
$\nu\{r\geq t:0<G(r)\leq u\}\leq u$ and the same calculation
with $A=G(t)$.  If $A=0$, both sides vanish; if $A=\infty$, the estimate is
immediate.  Sets on which the denominator is zero have measure zero
and are omitted.

Cauchy--Schwarz and \eqref{eq:Stieltjes-increasing} give
\[
 \left|\int_{[0,r]}f\,d\lambda\right|^2
 \leq2F(r)^{1/2}
 \int_{[0,r]}|f(t)|^2F(t)^{1/2}\,d\lambda(t).
\]
Moreover, \(F(r)^{1/2}\leq B_1^{1/2}G(r)^{-1/2}\), and hence
\begin{align*}
 \int_{[t,\infty)}F(r)^{1/2}\,d\nu(r)
 &\leq2B_1^{1/2}G(t)^{1/2}
 \leq2B_1F(t)^{-1/2}.
\end{align*}
Fubini therefore yields
\begin{align*}
 \|Hf\|_{L^2(\tau)}^2
 &\leq2\int_{[0,\infty)}|f(t)|^2F(t)^{1/2}
 \left[\int_{[t,\infty)}F(r)^{1/2}\,d\nu(r)\right]
d\lambda(t)
 \leq4B_1\|f\|_{L^2(\lambda)}^2.
\end{align*}
Taking \(f=1\) proves the first inequality.

For the second inequality, put
\[
Tf(r)=\int_{[r,\infty)}t^{-s}f(t)\,d\lambda(t).
\]
The adjoint is
\[
T^*g(t)=t^{-s}\int_{[0,t]}g(r)\,d\tau(r).
\]
Apply the first Hardy inequality to \(T^*\), with the roles of the
measures interchanged.  The resulting Muckenhoupt quantity is \(B_2\),
so \(\|T^*\|^2\leq4B_2\).  Since \(\|T\|=\|T^*\|\), taking \(f=1\)
gives the second estimate.  The intervals in
\eqref{eq:Stieltjes-increasing}--\eqref{eq:Stieltjes-decreasing} include
their endpoints as written.  Thus boundary atoms are assigned
consistently with the two kernels above.

The condition \eqref{eq:Hardy-no-common-zero} removes the only singular
common endpoint.  We only need to discuss a possible \(\tau\)-atom at
zero.
If \(\tau(\{0\})>0\), the contribution at \(r=0\) to the second
inequality also follows from
\[
 \left(\int_{(0,\infty)}t^{-s}\,d\lambda(t)\right)^2
 \leq\lambda([0,\infty))
 \int_{(0,\infty)}t^{-2s}\,d\lambda(t)
\]
and the limit as \(\rho\downarrow0\) in the definition of \(B_2\).

label: lem:local-tripled
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:local-tripled}
Let \(P=Q_S\) be the auxiliary quasicube from
\cref{lem:axis-sections}, and assume \(3P\cap\operatorname{supp}\widetilde\omega\subset L_0\). Then
\begin{align}
 &\int_{3P}\left|
 \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_P\widetilde\omega)
 \right|^2d\widetilde\sigma
 \leq C\left[
 \bigl(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\bigr)^2
 +\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega)
 +\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega)
 \right]\widetilde\omega(P).
 \label{eq:local-tripled}
\end{align}
Here
\[
 \mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 =\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n},\Omega}^{\mathrm{dual}}
   (\widetilde\sigma,\widetilde\omega)
\]
is the testing constant for the unrestricted pair over
\(\Omega\mathcal Q^n\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(s=n-\alpha\).  Fix one of the tangent-line truncations used in
\(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\).  Its radial multiplier
is symmetric, and its truncated kernel satisfies the same size bound,
with a uniform constant.  Moreover, \((\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n})^*(x,y) =\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(y,x) =-\mathbf K_\Psi^{\alpha,n}(x,y)\). All constants below are independent of the inner and outer truncation
radii.

The quasicube \(3P\) is the disjoint union of the images of \(3^n\)
half-open cubes of side \(\ell(P)\).  On \(P\), unrestricted dual testing
gives
\[
 \int_P\left|\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}
   (\mathbf 1_P\widetilde\omega)\right|^2d\widetilde\sigma
 \leq
 \bigl(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\bigr)^2
 \widetilde\omega(P).
\]

Let \(E\) be one of the other members of this partition.  Write
\(P=\Omega C\), \(E=\Omega D\), and
\(P\cap L_0=[a,b)e_1\).  Put
\(p_-=ae_1\), \(p_+=be_1\), and
\(\zeta(t)=\Omega^{-1}(te_1)\).  By the construction in
\cref{lem:axis-sections}, \(\ell(C)=8C_n(b-a)\). The path \(\zeta([a,b])\) meets only the first lower face, at
\(\zeta(a)\), and the second upper face, at \(\zeta(b)\).  Its
distance from every other face is at least \(c\ell(P)\).

There is a unique \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(D=C+\ell(C)m\).  If \(m_1=-1\), assign \(E\) to
\(p_-\).  For
\(x=te_1\in P\cap L_0\), \(y\in E\), and
\(\eta=\Omega^{-1}y\),
\begin{align*}
c_n|x-p_-|
 &\leq \zeta_1(t)-\zeta_1(a)
 \leq \zeta_1(t)-\eta_1
 \leq |\zeta(t)-\eta|
 \leq \operatorname{Lip}(\Omega^{-1})|x-y|.
\end{align*}
The triangle inequality then gives
\(|y-p_-|\leq C|x-y|\).  Suppose next that \(m_1\neq-1\) and
\(m_2=1\).  Assign \(E\) to \(p_+\).  The second coordinate gives
\begin{align*}
c_n|x-p_+|
 &\leq \zeta_2(b)-\zeta_2(t)
 \leq \eta_2-\zeta_2(t)
 \leq |\zeta(t)-\eta|
 \leq \operatorname{Lip}(\Omega^{-1})|x-y|.
\end{align*}
Thus \(|y-p_+|\leq C|x-y|\).

It remains to consider \(m_1\in\{0,1\},\quad m_2\in\{-1,0\},\quad m\neq0\). If \(m_1=1\), the first upper face separates \(D\) from the path.  If
\(m_2=-1\), the second lower face does so.  If
\(m_k\neq0\) for some \(3\leq k\leq n\), one of the two \(k\)-th
faces does so.  The face margins in \cref{lem:axis-sections} are at
least \(7\ell(C)/16\).  Hence every quasicube in this last class is
separated from \(P\cap L_0\) by \(c_\Omega\ell(P)\).  Its integral is
bounded by
\cref{lem:annular-A2}, applied to the finitely many annuli with radii
comparable to \(\ell(P)\).
In this separated application, the proof of \cref{lem:annular-A2} uses
only the one-tailed condition with the corresponding order of the two
measures; the punctured conditions are not used.

Fix one endpoint \(p\), and denote the corresponding Borel set by
\(E_p\).  The two preceding coordinate estimates and the triangle
inequality give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endpoint-cone-proof}
 |x-y|\geq c_0\bigl(|x-p|+|y-p|\bigr),
 \qquad x\in P\cap L_0,\quad y\in E_p,
\end{equation}
where \(c_0>0\) depends only on \(\Omega\).  Define measures on
\([0,\infty)\) by
\begin{align*}
 \lambda(B)
 &=\widetilde\omega
   \bigl(\{x\in P\cap L_0:|x-p|\in B\}\bigr),\\
 \tau(B)
 &=\widetilde\sigma
   \bigl(\{y\in E_p:|y-p|\in B\}\bigr).
\end{align*}
The half-open sets \(P\) and \(E_p\) are disjoint.  Thus \(p\) belongs
to at most one of them.  Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:no-common-radial-origin}
 \lambda(\{0\})\tau(\{0\})=0.
\end{equation}
Thus the hypothesis \eqref{eq:Hardy-no-common-zero} of
\cref{lem:Hardy} holds.
For \(r=|y-p|\), the kernel estimate and
\eqref{eq:endpoint-cone-proof} give
\begin{align}
 \left|\mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}
   (\mathbf 1_P\widetilde\omega)(y)\right|
 &\leq C\int_{[0,\infty)}(r+t)^{-s}\,d\lambda(t)
 \leq C\left[
r^{-s}\lambda([0,r])
 +\int_{[r,\infty)}t^{-s}\,d\lambda(t)
 \right].
 \label{eq:hardy-kernel-split}
\end{align}
If \(\tau(\{0\})>0\), then
\eqref{eq:no-common-radial-origin} gives
\(\lambda(\{0\})=0\).  At \(r=0\), we therefore read the first term as
zero and the second as \(\int_{(0,\infty)}t^{-s}\,d\lambda(t)\).

It remains to bound \(B_1\) and \(B_2\) in \cref{lem:Hardy}.  Recall that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal P^\alpha(H,\nu)
 =\int_{\mathbb R^n}
 \left(
  \frac{|H|^{1/n}}
  {\bigl(|H|^{1/n}+|z-c_H|\bigr)^2}
 \right)^s d\nu(z).
\end{equation*}
Thus
\begin{align}
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha
 &=\sup_{H\in\Omega\mathcal Q^n}
 \frac{\widetilde\omega(H)}{|H|^{s/n}}
 \mathcal P^\alpha
   (H,\mathbf 1_{H^c}\widetilde\sigma),
 \label{eq:one-tail-forward-local}\\
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}
 &=\sup_{H\in\Omega\mathcal Q^n}
 \frac{\widetilde\sigma(H)}{|H|^{s/n}}
 \mathcal P^\alpha
   (H,\mathbf 1_{H^c}\widetilde\omega).
 \label{eq:one-tail-dual-local}
\end{align}
The estimates below use the reproducing Poisson integral
\(\mathcal P^\alpha\).

Both \(P\cap L_0\) and \(E_p\) are contained in a ball
\(B(p,C_1\ell(P))\).  Hence the expressions defining the Hardy
constants vanish when \(\rho>C_1\ell(P)\).  We may therefore fix
\(0<\rho\leq C_1\ell(P)\).

We first estimate
\[
B_1(\rho)
 :=\lambda([0,\rho])
   \int_{[\rho,\infty)}r^{-2s}\,d\tau(r).
\]
Let \(S_{\rho,p}\subset L_0\) be the half-open interval of length
\(2\rho\) which starts at \(p\) when \(p\in P\), and which ends at
\(p\) when \(p\notin P\).  Then \(\{x\in P\cap L_0:|x-p|\leq\rho\}\subset S_{\rho,p}\). Let \(H_\rho=Q_{S_{\rho,p}}\) be the quasicube supplied by
\cref{lem:axis-sections}.  The construction in that lemma gives \(\ell(H_\rho)\approx_\Omega\rho, \quad H_\rho\subset B(p,C_2\rho), \quad |c_{H_\rho}-p|\leq C_2\rho\). Choose \(C_0>4C_2\).  If \(y\in E_p\) and
\(|y-p|\geq C_0\rho\), then \(y\in H_\rho^c\),
\(|y-c_{H_\rho}|\approx|y-p|\), and
\begin{equation*}
 |y-p|^{-2s}
 \leq C\rho^{-s}
 \left(
  \frac{|H_\rho|^{1/n}}
  {\bigl(|H_\rho|^{1/n}+|y-c_{H_\rho}|\bigr)^2}
 \right)^s.
\end{equation*}
The factor \(\lambda([0,\rho])\) is bounded by
\(\widetilde\omega(H_\rho)\), while the part of
\(\widetilde\sigma\) in the integral is supported in \(H_\rho^c\).
Therefore
\begin{align}
 &\lambda([0,\rho])
 \int_{[C_0\rho,\infty)}r^{-2s}\,d\tau(r)\leq
C\frac{\widetilde\omega(H_\rho)}{|H_\rho|^{s/n}}
 \mathcal P^\alpha
   (H_\rho,\mathbf 1_{H_\rho^c}\widetilde\sigma)
 \leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha.
 \label{eq:B1-far}
\end{align}

It remains to treat \([\rho,C_0\rho)\).  Put
\begin{align*}
X_\rho^0&=\{x\in P\cap L_0:|x-p|\leq\rho\},\qquad
Y_\rho^1=\{y\in E_p:\rho\leq|y-p|<C_0\rho\}.
\end{align*}
By \eqref{eq:endpoint-cone-proof},
\(\operatorname{dist}(X_\rho^0,Y_\rho^1)\geq c_0\rho\).  Choose
\(0<\delta<c_0/(10\sqrt n\operatorname{Lip}(\Omega))\).  Partition the
preimage space into half-open cubes of side \(\delta\rho\).  Let
\(\mathcal U_\rho\) be the images under \(\Omega\) of the cubes which
meet \(X_\rho^0\), and let \(\mathcal V_\rho\) be those which meet
\(Y_\rho^1\).  Each family has at most \(N=N(n,\Omega,C_0)\) members.
No member of one family is a member of the other.  Thus every
\(U\in\mathcal U_\rho\) and \(V\in\mathcal V_\rho\) is a pair of
disjoint quasicubes, and \(\ell(U)=\ell(V)=\delta\rho, \quad |z-c_U|\leq C\rho\quad(z\in V)\). Consequently, \(\mathcal P^\alpha(U,\mathbf 1_{U^c}\widetilde\sigma) \geq c\frac{|U|^{s/n}}{\rho^{2s}} \widetilde\sigma(V)\). By \eqref{eq:one-tail-forward-local}, \(\rho^{-2s}\widetilde\omega(U)\widetilde\sigma(V) \leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha\). Summing over at most \(N^2\) pairs gives
\begin{align}
 &\lambda([0,\rho])
 \int_{[\rho,C_0\rho)}r^{-2s}\,d\tau(r)\leq
 \rho^{-2s}
 \widetilde\omega(X_\rho^0)
 \widetilde\sigma(Y_\rho^1)
 \leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha.
 \label{eq:B1-middle}
\end{align}
Equations \eqref{eq:B1-far} and \eqref{eq:B1-middle} show that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:B1-bound}
B_1\leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha.
\end{equation}

We next estimate
\[
B_2(\rho)
 :=\tau([0,\rho])
   \int_{[\rho,\infty)}t^{-2s}\,d\lambda(t).
\]
Partition the preimage space into half-open cubes of side \(\rho\), and
let \(\mathcal H_\rho\) be the images under \(\Omega\) of the cubes
which meet \(Y_\rho^0=\{y\in E_p:|y-p|\leq\rho\}\). There are at most \(N_0=N_0(n,\Omega)\) such quasicubes.  Each
\(H\in\mathcal H_\rho\) satisfies \(\ell(H)=\rho,\quad H\subset B(p,C_3\rho),\quad |c_H-p|\leq C_3\rho\). Choose \(C_4>4C_3\).  Then the source
set \(\{x\in P\cap L_0:|x-p|\geq C_4\rho\}\) lies in \(H^c\) for every
\(H\in\mathcal H_\rho\), and \(|x-p|^{-2s} \leq C\rho^{-s} \left( \frac{|H|^{1/n}} {\bigl(|H|^{1/n}+|x-c_H|\bigr)^2} \right)^s\). The set \(Y_\rho^0\) is covered by \(\mathcal H_\rho\), while
\(\{x\in P\cap L_0:|x-p|\geq C_4\rho\}\subset H^c\) for every
\(H\in\mathcal H_\rho\).  Hence
\begin{align}
 &\tau([0,\rho])
 \int_{[C_4\rho,\infty)}t^{-2s}\,d\lambda(t)\leq
C\sum_{H\in\mathcal H_\rho}
 \frac{\widetilde\sigma(H)}{|H|^{s/n}}
 \mathcal P^\alpha
   (H,\mathbf 1_{H^c}\widetilde\omega)
 \leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}.
 \label{eq:B2-far}
\end{align}

For the intermediate part, put \(X_\rho^1 =\{x\in P\cap L_0:\rho\leq|x-p|<C_4\rho\}\). The sets \(X_\rho^1\) and \(Y_\rho^0\) are separated by
\(c_0\rho\).  Repeat the half-open grid construction above, with
quasicubes of side \(\delta\rho\).  The two resulting families have at
most \(N_1=N_1(n,\Omega,C_4)\) members.  If \(U\) meets \(X_\rho^1\) and
\(V\) meets \(Y_\rho^0\), then \(U\cap V=\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal P^\alpha(V,\mathbf 1_{V^c}\widetilde\omega) \geq c\frac{|V|^{s/n}}{\rho^{2s}} \widetilde\omega(U)\). The dual one-tailed condition gives \(\rho^{-2s}\widetilde\sigma(V)\widetilde\omega(U) \leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}\). After summing over the finitely many pairs,
\begin{align*}
 &\tau([0,\rho])
 \int_{[\rho,C_4\rho)}t^{-2s}\,d\lambda(t)\leq
 \rho^{-2s}
 \widetilde\sigma(Y_\rho^0)
 \widetilde\omega(X_\rho^1)
 \leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}.
\end{align*}
Together with \eqref{eq:B2-far}, this proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:B2-bound}
B_2\leq C\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}.
\end{equation}
The constant in \eqref{eq:B1-bound} and \eqref{eq:B2-bound} depends only
on \(n\), \(\alpha\), the biLipschitz constants of \(\Omega\), and the
constants in \eqref{eq:coordinate-monotonicity}.  It is independent of
\(P\), \(p\), \(\rho\), and the truncation parameters.

It remains to check atoms on the half-open boundaries.  By
\eqref{eq:no-common-radial-origin}, no common atom occurs on both sides
of the singular Hardy kernel.  The quasicubes used above are also
half-open.  An atom on a boundary belongs to one member of the
partition, and the complementary measure in
\eqref{eq:one-tail-forward-local} or
\eqref{eq:one-tail-dual-local} lies in the corresponding hole.  Thus
\eqref{eq:B1-bound} and \eqref{eq:B2-bound} include endpoint atoms.

Applying \cref{lem:Hardy} to \eqref{eq:hardy-kernel-split} yields
\[
 \int_{E_p}\left|
 \mathbf R_\Psi^{\alpha,n}
   (\mathbf 1_P\widetilde\omega)
 \right|^2d\widetilde\sigma
 \leq C\left(
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha
 +\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}
 \right)\widetilde\omega(P).
\]
Apply this estimate to the two endpoint unions.  Add the unrestricted
testing estimate on \(P\) and the estimates for the finitely many
separated members of the partition of \(3P\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:local-tripled}.
