Choose the decomposition in \cref{lem:nested-arcs} with
\(A>2C_{\rm ax}\), where \(C_{\rm ax}\) is fixed by
\eqref{eq:axis-family-constant}.  Fix \(i\), and put \(\Omega=\Omega_i=\Psi_i^{-1}\circ R_i\), where \(R_i\) is the rotation used in
\eqref{eq:coordinate-monotonicity}.  Thus \(\Omega\) satisfies the
hypothesis of \cref{lem:axis-sections}.  Work in the rigid coordinates
of the $i$-th arc, and denote $(\mathcal U_i)_\#\sigma$ and
$(\mathcal U_i)_\#\omega$ again by $\sigma$ and $\omega$.  Put
\[
 \widetilde\sigma_i=\Psi_i^*\sigma,\qquad
 \widetilde\omega^{(i)}=\Psi_i^*\omega,\qquad
 \widetilde\omega_i=\Psi_i^*(\mathbf 1_{\Gamma_i}\omega).
\]
In this proposition,
\(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}\),
\(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\), and the
Muckenhoupt constants refer to the unrestricted pair
\((\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega^{(i)})\) over
\(\Omega\mathcal Q^n\).  Then, for every
\(Q\in\Omega\mathcal Q^n\),
\begin{align}
 \int_Q\left|
 \mathbf R_{\Psi_i}^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_Q\widetilde\omega_i)
 \right|^2d\widetilde\sigma_i
 &\leq C\left[
 \bigl(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\bigr)^2
 +\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha
 +\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}
 \right]\widetilde\omega_i(Q),
 \label{eq:localized-dual-testing}\\
 \int_Q\left|
 \mathbf R_{\Psi_i}^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_Q\widetilde\sigma_i)
 \right|^2d\widetilde\omega_i
 &\leq
 \bigl(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{full}}\bigr)^2
 \widetilde\sigma_i(Q).\notag
\end{align}
There is no restriction on \(\ell(Q)\).

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(\omega_E=\mathbf 1_E\omega\), let \(\mathfrak P\) be the common atoms
of \((\sigma,\omega)\), and let
\(\mathfrak P_E=\mathfrak P\cap E\).  The two one-tailed constants are
monotone:
\[
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\sigma,\omega_E)
 \leq\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^\alpha(\sigma,\omega),
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}(\sigma,\omega_E)
 \leq\mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}(\sigma,\omega).
\]
It remains to consider the two punctured products
\[
 \frac{\sigma(Q,\mathfrak P_E)\omega_E(Q)}
 {|Q|^{2(1-\alpha/n)}}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac{\sigma(Q)\omega_E(Q,\mathfrak P_E)}
 {|Q|^{2(1-\alpha/n)}}.
\]
Fix an \(\Omega\)-quasicube \(Q\).  If
\(Q\cap\mathfrak P=\varnothing\), both products decrease under the
restriction.  We therefore assume that
\(Q\cap\mathfrak P\neq\varnothing\).

We first record an elementary fact.  If \(\mu(Q)<\infty\), the
\(\mu\)-masses of any nonempty collection of atoms in \(Q\) have a
maximum.  Indeed, if the supremum \(M>0\) were not attained, infinitely
many distinct atoms would have mass greater than \(M/2\), contradicting
\(\mu(Q)<\infty\).

Choose \(p\in Q\cap\mathfrak P\) such that \(\sigma(\{p\}) =\max_{q\in Q\cap\mathfrak P}\sigma(\{q\})\). If \(p\in E\), then \(p\) is also a largest common
\(\sigma\)-atom for the restricted pair.  Hence
\(\sigma(Q,\mathfrak P_E)=\sigma(Q,\mathfrak P)\), and the first
punctured product is bounded by
\(A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,\mathrm{punct}}(\sigma,\omega)\).

Suppose that \(p\notin E\).  Then \(\sigma(Q,\mathfrak P_E) \leq\sigma(Q,\mathfrak P)+\sigma(\{p\})\). After division by \(|Q|^{2(1-\alpha/n)}\), the term
\(\sigma(Q,\mathfrak P)\omega_E(Q)\) is bounded by
\(A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,\mathrm{punct}}(\sigma,\omega)\).
Choose \(r\in Q\cap\mathfrak P\) such that \(\omega(\{r\}) =\max_{q\in Q\cap\mathfrak P}\omega(\{q\})\). We write
\[
 \sigma(\{p\})\omega_E(Q)
 =
 \sigma(\{p\})
 \bigl[\omega_E(Q)-\mathbf 1_E(r)\omega(\{r\})\bigr]
 +\mathbf 1_E(r)\sigma(\{p\})\omega(\{r\}).
\]
The expression in brackets is at most
\(\omega(Q)-\omega(\{r\})=\omega(Q,\mathfrak P)\).  Since
\(\sigma(\{p\})\leq\sigma(Q)\), division by
\(|Q|^{2(1-\alpha/n)}\) shows that the first term is bounded by the
original starred punctured characteristic
\(A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}(\sigma,\omega)\).

If \(r=p\), the last term vanishes because \(p\notin E\).  It remains
to consider \(r\in E\) and \(r\neq p\).  Put \(a=\Omega^{-1}(p),\quad b=\Omega^{-1}(r),\quad d=|a-b|_\infty\), and let
\[
C=\prod_{k=1}^n[a_k-d/4,a_k+d/4),
 \qquad H=\Omega C.
\]
Then \(p\in H\), \(r\notin H\), and \(\ell(H)=d/2,\quad |H|^{1/n}\approx_\Omega d,\quad |p-r|\approx_\Omega d\). Therefore the starred one-tailed condition with a hole gives
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}(\sigma,\omega)
 &\geq
 \frac{\sigma(H)}{|H|^{1-\alpha/n}}
 \mathcal P^\alpha(H,\mathbf 1_{H^c}\omega)\gtrsim_\Omega
 \frac{\sigma(\{p\})\omega(\{r\})}
 {d^{2(n-\alpha)}}.
\end{align*}
Since \(p,r\in Q\), their preimages belong to the ordinary cube
\(\Omega^{-1}Q\).  Thus \(d\leq\ell(Q)\), while
\(|Q|^{1/n}\approx_\Omega\ell(Q)\).  It follows that
\[
 \frac{\sigma(\{p\})\omega(\{r\})}
 {|Q|^{2(1-\alpha/n)}}
 \lesssim_\Omega
 \mathcal A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*}(\sigma,\omega).
\]
This proves the required estimate for the unstarred punctured
characteristic of the restricted pair.

The starred punctured characteristic is termwise monotone.  Indeed,
let \(r\) be a largest common \(\omega\)-atom of the full pair in
\(Q\).  If \(r\in E\), it remains a largest common \(\omega\)-atom
after restriction, and \(\omega_E(Q,\mathfrak P_E) =\omega_E(Q)-\omega(\{r\}) \leq\omega(Q)-\omega(\{r\}) =\omega(Q,\mathfrak P)\). If \(r\notin E\), then \(\omega_E(Q,\mathfrak P_E) \leq\omega_E(Q) \leq\omega(Q)-\omega(\{r\}) =\omega(Q,\mathfrak P)\). Multiplication by
\(\sigma(Q)/|Q|^{2(1-\alpha/n)}\) gives
\[
A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}(\sigma,\omega_E)
 \leq
A_{2,\Omega}^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}(\sigma,\omega).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:A2-restriction}.

body_md:
For \(n=1\), a compact regular curve is an interval, so
\cite[Theorem~9]{CurvePaper} applies directly.  We now assume
\(n\geq2\).
By duality, suppose that $\omega$ is supported on the regular
$C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $\Gamma=\Phi([a,b])$.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Step 1: finite graph pieces.}
The goodness exponent \(\varepsilon\) fixed after
\eqref{eq:strong-energy-definition} and the slope bound for the graph
charts are independent parameters.  Put \(\varepsilon_{\rm sl}:=\frac12\varepsilon_{n,\alpha}\). We follow the order of choices in \cref{lem:nested-arcs}.  First choose
its finite graph-chart family, before choosing \(A\).  In the rigid
coordinates of a chart indexed by \(\nu\),
write the two graph-coordinate intervals used for the extension as \(\widehat J_\nu^0\Subset J_\nu^*, \ \operatorname{dist}(\widehat J_\nu^0,\mathbb R\setminus J_\nu^*) \geq\kappa|J_\nu^*|\). Let \(\psi_\nu^*\) denote the local graph function on \(J_\nu^*\).
Translate in the transverse direction so that
\(\psi_\nu^*(t_\nu)=0\) at some \(t_\nu\in J_\nu^*\).  Uniform
continuity of
\(\Phi'\) makes the chart small enough that \(\|D\psi_\nu^*\|_\infty<\varepsilon_{\rm sl}/C_\kappa\), where \(C_\kappa\) is the constant in
\cref{lem:graph-extension}.
\Cref{lem:graph-modulus} gives \(\vartheta_{\psi_\nu^*}(r) \leq C\vartheta_\Phi(Cr), \quad 0<r\leq c\). The part of the Dini integral over \([c,1]\) is finite because
\(D\psi_\nu^*\) is bounded.
\Cref{lem:graph-extension} gives
\(\psi_\nu\in C_c^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^{n-1})\), equal to
\(\psi_\nu^*\) on \(\widehat J_\nu^0\), such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:small-extended-graph}
 \|D\psi_\nu\|_\infty<\varepsilon_{n,\alpha},\qquad
 \|\psi_\nu\|_\infty
 \leq C_\kappa\varepsilon_{\rm sl}|J_\nu^*|.
\end{equation}
Let \(\Psi_\nu(x_1,x')=(x_1,x'+\psi_\nu(x_1))\). These finitely many maps fix the constants \(K\) and \(C_{\rm ax}\) in
\eqref{eq:axis-family-constant}.  Now choose \(A>2C_{\rm ax}\) and form
the final arcs in \cref{lem:nested-arcs}.  Let \(\Psi_i\) be the fixed
map and let \(\mathcal U_i\) be the rigid motion assigned there to
\(\Gamma_i\).
The map \(\Psi_i\) sends the relevant interval of \(L_0\) onto the graph
arc, and \(\Psi_i,\Psi_i^{-1}\) are globally biLipschitz.

Put \(\omega_i=\mathbf 1_{\Gamma_i}\omega\).  The half-open convention in
\cref{lem:nested-arcs}, including the cyclic convention for a closed
curve, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:measure-decomposition}
 \omega=\sum_{i=1}^N\omega_i.
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Step 2: testing after straightening.}
Fix \(i\).  Pass to its rigid graph coordinates by defining
\[
 \sigma_i^{\rm rig}=(\mathcal U_i)_\#\sigma,
 \qquad
 \omega^{(i),\rm rig}=(\mathcal U_i)_\#\omega,
 \qquad
 \omega_i^{\rm rig}=(\mathcal U_i)_\#\omega_i.
\]
For Steps 2--4 with this fixed \(i\), we denote these three measures
again by \(\sigma\), \(\omega\), and \(\omega_i\).  We restore the
original coordinates before summing in \(i\).  Let \(R_i\) be the
diagonal rotation fixed for this chart in the proof of
\cref{lem:nested-arcs}, and put \(\Omega_i=\Psi_i^{-1}\circ R_i\). The fractional Riesz vector is covariant under rigid motions.  Its
Euclidean vector norm and vector testing are unchanged, while the
combined Muckenhoupt constants are comparable with dimensional
constants.  A cube \(R_iQ\) in the rigid graph coordinates
corresponds to the rotated cube \(\mathcal U_i^{-1}(R_iQ)\) in the
original coordinates; the translation in \(\mathcal U_i\) only changes
the center.  Therefore the hypothesis over all rotated cubes gives
unrestricted testing for the relabeled pair over
\(R_i\mathcal Q^n\).  Put
\[
 \widetilde\sigma_i=\Psi_i^*\sigma,
 \qquad
 \widetilde\omega^{(i)}=\Psi_i^*\omega,
 \qquad
 \widetilde\omega_i=\Psi_i^*\omega_i.
\]
Then \(\widetilde\omega_i\) is supported on \(L_0\), and \(\Psi_i^{-1}(R_i\mathcal Q^n)=\Omega_i\mathcal Q^n\). \Cref{prop:change-variable} gives unrestricted conformal testing for
\((\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega^{(i)})\) over this family.  The
cutoff comparison is uniform in the inner and outer
truncation radii.  The combined Muckenhoupt comparison is
\eqref{eq:A2-pullback}.

\Cref{prop:localized-testing} gives testing for the restricted
pulled-back pair over all testing quasicubes.  The measure identity
\eqref{eq:exact-measure-localization} includes atoms at partition
boundaries.  Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:localized-testing}
 \mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_{\Psi_i}^{\alpha,n},\Omega_i}
   (\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega_i)
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R_{\Psi_i}^{\alpha,n},\Omega_i}^{\mathrm{dual}}
   (\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega_i)
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \right).
\end{equation}
\Cref{lem:A2-restriction} and the combined pullback estimate also give
\[
 \mathfrak A_{2,\Omega_i}^\alpha
 (\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega_i)
 \leq C\mathfrak A_2^\alpha(\sigma,\omega).
\]
Applying \cref{prop:change-variable} in the reverse direction gives
testing for \((\sigma,\omega_i)\) over \(R_i\mathcal Q^n\).  Write
\(\mathfrak T_i\) and \(\mathfrak T_i^{\mathrm{dual}}\) for these two
restricted testing constants.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:restricted-original-testing}
 \mathfrak T_i+\mathfrak T_i^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \right).
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Step 3: energy on the line and transfer back.}
Apply \cref{prop:C1-energy-reversal}, using
\eqref{eq:small-extended-graph} and
\eqref{eq:localized-testing}, with the quasicube map
\(\Omega_i=\Psi_i^{-1}\circ R_i\).  The pulled-back pair satisfies the
forward and dual strong-energy conditions of
\cite[Definition~5]{EnergyCommon}:
\begin{align*}
 &\mathcal E_{\alpha,\Omega_i}^{\mathrm{strong}}
   (\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega_i)
 +\mathcal E_{\alpha,\Omega_i}^{\mathrm{strong,dual}}
   (\widetilde\sigma_i,\widetilde\omega_i)
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \right).
\end{align*}
This includes the supremum over every dyadic grid and subpartition, the
alternate-top expression, and every refinement index \(\ell\).
\Cref{prop:energy-invariance}, with \(F=\Psi_i,\quad \widetilde\Omega_i=F^{-1}\circ R_i=\Omega_i\), transfers these estimates to
\[
 \mathcal E_{\alpha,R_i}^{\mathrm{strong}}(\sigma,\omega_i)
 +\mathcal E_{\alpha,R_i}^{\mathrm{strong,dual}}(\sigma,\omega_i)
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\right).
\]
We can therefore apply the \(T1\) theorem in the original coordinates.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Step 4: apply the $T1$ theorem to the smooth kernel.}
Fix \(i\) and put \(\Omega=R_i\).  For the pair
\((\sigma,\omega_i)\), the preceding steps give
\begin{align*}
 &\mathcal A_{2,R_i}^\alpha
 +\mathcal A_{2,R_i}^{\alpha,*}
 +A_{2,R_i}^{\alpha,\mathrm{punct}}
 +A_{2,R_i}^{\alpha,*,\mathrm{punct}}<\infty,\\
 &\mathcal E_{\alpha,R_i}^{\mathrm{strong}}
 +\mathcal E_{\alpha,R_i}^{\mathrm{strong,dual}}<\infty.
\end{align*}
The energy constants are uniform over every dyadic quasigrid
\(R_i\mathcal D\).  They include the subpartition, alternate-top, and
refined families in \cite[Definition~5]{EnergyCommon}.

For every \(Q\in R_i\mathcal Q^n\) and \(1\leq j\leq n\), vector
testing gives
\begin{align*}
 \int_Q|R_{j,\sigma}^{\alpha,n}(\mathbf 1_Q)|^2\,d\omega_i
 &\leq\mathfrak T_i^2\sigma(Q),\\
 \int_Q|R_{j,\omega_i}^{\alpha,n,*}(\mathbf 1_Q)|^2\,d\sigma
 &\leq(\mathfrak T_i^{\mathrm{dual}})^2\omega_i(Q).
\end{align*}
Thus both scalar quasicube testing conditions hold, and
\eqref{eq:restricted-original-testing} gives their required bounds.
The constants in these two displays use the tangent-line truncations.
Denote the corresponding scalar smooth testing constants by
\(\mathfrak T_{i,j}^{s}\) and
\(\mathfrak T_{i,j}^{s,\mathrm{dual}}\).  By
\eqref{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison}, they satisfy
\[
 \mathfrak T_{i,j}^{s}
 +\mathfrak T_{i,j}^{s,\mathrm{dual}}
 \leq C\left(
 \mathfrak T_i+\mathfrak T_i^{\mathrm{dual}}
 +\sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}\right).
\]
Here we apply \cref{lem:tangent-smooth-comparison} to
\(K_j^{\alpha,n}\), with a constant independent of \(j\).

The scalar Riesz kernel in the current rigid coordinates is \(K_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y) =c_{\alpha,n}\frac{y_j-x_j}{|y-x|^{n+1-\alpha}}\). Direct differentiation gives
\begin{align*}
 |K_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|
 &\leq C|x-y|^{\alpha-n},\\
 |\nabla_xK_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|
 +|\nabla_yK_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y)|
 &\leq C|x-y|^{\alpha-n-1}.
\end{align*}
If \(|x-x'|\leq|x-y|/2\), the mean value theorem applied to the second
derivatives gives
\[
 |\nabla_xK_j^{\alpha,n}(x,y)-\nabla_xK_j^{\alpha,n}(x',y)|
 \leq C|x-x'|\,|x-y|^{\alpha-n-2}.
\]
The analogous estimate holds in the \(y\)-variable and for the adjoint
kernel.  Thus this is a standard \(\alpha\)-fractional
Calder\'on--Zygmund kernel of smoothness exponent \(\delta=1\).  Its
constants depend only on \(n\) and \(\alpha\).  Therefore
\cite[Theorem~2]{GoodLambda}, with
\(T^\alpha=R_j^{\alpha,n}\) and \(\Omega=R_i\), applies to
\((\sigma,\omega_i)\).  Its hypotheses are the four Muckenhoupt
conditions, the two quasitesting conditions, and the two strong
quasienergy conditions verified above.  It gives
\[
 \mathfrak N_{R_j^{\alpha,n}}^{s}(\sigma,\omega_i)
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\right).
\]
By \eqref{eq:smooth-tangent-comparison}, the tangent-line norm satisfies
\[
 \mathfrak N_{R_j^{\alpha,n}}(\sigma,\omega_i)
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}\right).
\]
Since
\[
 \|\mathbf R_\sigma^{\alpha,n}f\|_{L^2(\omega_i;\ell^2)}^2
 =\sum_{j=1}^n
 \|R_{j,\sigma}^{\alpha,n}f\|_{L^2(\omega_i)}^2,
\]
we obtain
\begin{equation*}
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}(\sigma,\omega_i)
 \leq C\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \right).
\end{equation*}
Returning to the original coordinates gives the same estimate for
\((\sigma,\omega_i)\).  By \eqref{eq:measure-decomposition},
\begin{align*}
 \|\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}_\sigma f\|_{L^2(\omega)}^2
 &=\sum_{i=1}^N
   \|\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}_\sigma f\|_{L^2(\omega_i)}^2
 \leq C_N\left(
 \sqrt{\mathfrak A_2^\alpha}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \right)^2
 \|f\|_{L^2(\sigma)}^2.
\end{align*}
This proves sufficiency.

We finish with necessity.  Fix any tangent-line truncation
\(\mathbf R_{\varepsilon,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}\) used in the definition of the
operator norm.  Its kernel is zero on the diagonal.  Hence, for every
rotated cube \(Q\),
\[
 \int_Q
 \left|\mathbf R_{\varepsilon,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}(\mathbf 1_Q\sigma)\right|^2
d\omega
 \leq
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^2\sigma(Q).
\]
For each \(1\leq j\leq n\), the \(j\)-th truncated scalar component
has operator norm at most \(\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}\), and
Hilbert space duality gives the same bound for its adjoint.  Summing the
squared \(L^2(\sigma)\) norms of the \(n\) adjoint components gives
\[
 \int_Q
 \left|
 \bigl(\mathbf R_{\varepsilon,R}^{\alpha,n,\mathrm{tl}}\bigr)^*
 (\mathbf 1_Q\omega)\right|^2d\sigma
 \leq
n\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^2\omega(Q).
\]
These estimates are uniform in \(\varepsilon,R\).  Thus
\[
 \mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}
 +\mathfrak T_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^{\mathrm{dual}}
 \leq(1+\sqrt n)\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}.
\]

The necessity of the two one-tailed conditions with holes and the two
punctured conditions is proved in
\cite[Theorem~5(2)]{CurvePaper}; see also
\cite[Sections~2.2 and 2.2.1]{CurvePaper}.  That proof has no regularity
assumption on the support of either measure.  It applies to the
tangent-line truncations used here.  Each separated-set comparison in the
cited proof is first made on a bounded piece.  Choose
\(\varepsilon\) smaller than the separation and \(R\) larger than the
diameter of that piece.  The tangent-line multiplier is then one on the
relevant product.  The estimates are independent of \(\varepsilon\) and
\(R\).  Exhausting an unbounded tail by bounded pieces and using monotone
convergence for the positive Poisson expressions gives the full
one-tailed conditions.

For completeness, the fractional Riesz vector has the strong
ellipticity used for the one-tailed conditions.  Cover the unit sphere by
finitely many cones.  For each cone, one can choose a unit vector \(e\)
such that \(\left| e\cdot\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(x,y) \right| \geq c_{n,\alpha}|x-y|^{\alpha-n}\) whenever \(y-x\) belongs to that cone, and
\(e\cdot\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(x,y)\) does not change sign there.  The
punctured argument removes a largest common
point mass in each cube.  Since every truncated kernel is zero on the
diagonal, a common atom paired with itself makes no contribution.  Thus
the common-point-mass proof in
\cite[Section~2.2.1]{CurvePaper} gives \(\mathfrak A_2^\alpha \leq C\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{\alpha,n}}^2\).
The testing estimates are uniform over all rotations.  If
\(\rho(x)=Ux+a\), where \(U\) is orthogonal, then \(\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(\rho x,\rho y) =U\mathbf K^{\alpha,n}(x,y)\). The Euclidean norm of the vector kernel is unchanged.  Equivalently,
one may apply \cite[Theorem~5(2)]{CurvePaper} with each rigid motion
as the quasicube map; all its biLipschitz constants are one.  The
estimates are therefore uniform over all rotated cubes.  Together with
the testing estimates above, this proves necessity and the opposite
inequality in \eqref{eq:norm-comparison}.

The bound for \(B_\Omega\) and Cauchy--Schwarz give \(|\mathbf S_{\Omega,\sigma}f(x)| \leq C_{\Omega,\Gamma}\sigma(\Gamma)^{1/2} \|f\|_{L^2(\sigma)}\). Consequently,
\[
 \|\mathbf S_{\Omega,\sigma}f\|_{L^2(\omega)}
 \leq C_{\Omega,\Gamma}M_\Omega(\sigma,\omega)
       \|f\|_{L^2(\sigma)}.
\]
The transposed operator satisfies the same estimate.  For every rotated
cube \(Q\), we also have
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_Q|\mathbf S_{\Omega,\sigma}(\mathbf 1_Q)|^2d\omega
 &\leq C_{\Omega,\Gamma}^2\sigma(Q)^2\omega(Q)\\
 &\leq C_{\Omega,\Gamma}^2M_\Omega(\sigma,\omega)^2\sigma(Q).
 \end{split}
\]
After interchanging \(\sigma\) and \(\omega\), the same calculation
gives the dual testing estimate.

It follows that
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathfrak N_{\mathbf G_\Omega}
 &\leq |a_n|\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{1,n}}
       +C_{\Omega,\Gamma}M_\Omega,\\
 |a_n|\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{1,n}}
 &\leq \mathfrak N_{\mathbf G_\Omega}
       +C_{\Omega,\Gamma}M_\Omega.
 \end{split}
\]
The same two comparisons hold for the forward and dual testing
constants.  We now apply \cref{thm:main} with \(\alpha=1\).  It gives
the three stated conditions and the quantitative comparison.

label: cor:bounded-distance-power
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:bounded-distance-power}
Let \(d\sigma=ds_\Gamma=d\mathcal H^1|_\Gamma\), let
\(\beta>-(n-1)\), and let \(d\omega_\beta(x) :=\mathbf 1_{U_{\rho_0}}(x)d_\Gamma(x)^\beta\,dx\). Then \(\|\nabla u_f\|_{L^2(\omega_\beta)} \leq C_\beta\|f\|_{L^2(ds_\Gamma)}\) holds for every \(f\in L^2(ds_\Gamma)\) if and only if \(\beta>n-3\). Here \(u_f\) is the Dirichlet solution of \(-\Delta u_f=f\,ds_\Gamma\quad\text{in }\Omega, \quad u_f=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega\). In particular, for a curve source in \(\mathbb R^3\), the exact range is
\(\beta>0\).  At \(\beta=0\), the test density used below gives logarithmic
divergence.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove sufficiency.  Partition the target tube into finitely many
smaller graph boxes subordinate to enlarged graph neighbourhoods of the
kind constructed in \cref{lem:nested-arcs}.  The part of the curve that
can approach one of these boxes lies in its enlarged graph neighbourhood;
all other pieces of the curve are separated from the box.  After a rigid
motion, the curve in one such neighbourhood has the form \(y=(t,\psi(t)),\quad t\in J\), where \(\|\psi'\|_\infty\) is small.  In a smaller neighbourhood write \(x=(s,\psi(s)+z),\quad z\in\mathbb R^{n-1}\). The Jacobian of this change of variables is one.  The nested-arc
separation in \cref{lem:nested-arcs} and the small slope give \(d_\Gamma(x)\approx|z|, \quad |x-y|\approx\bigl(|s-t|^2+|z|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\). The arc-length density
\((1+|\psi'(t)|^2)^{1/2}\) is bounded above and below.

Extend \(f\) by zero in the tangential variable.  For fixed
\(z\neq0\), the kernel size estimate and Young's inequality give
\[
 \|\mathbf R^{1,n}_{ds_\Gamma}f(\cdot,z)\|_{L_s^2}
 \leq C\|k_{|z|}\|_{L^1}\|f\|_{L^2(ds_\Gamma)},
 \qquad
k_\rho(t):=\mathbf 1_{[-C,C]}(t)(t^2+\rho^2)^{(1-n)/2}.
\]
For \(0<\rho<\rho_0\),
\[
 \|k_\rho\|_{L^1}
 \leq
 \begin{cases}
C\rho^{2-n},&n\geq3,\\
C\log(e/\rho),&n=2.
 \end{cases}
\]
When \(n\geq3\), polar coordinates in \(\mathbb R^{n-1}\) give
\[
 \int_{|z|<\rho_0}|z|^\beta\|k_{|z|}\|_{L^1}^2\,dz
 \leq C\int_0^{\rho_0}\rho^{\beta+2-n}\,d\rho.
\]
This is finite exactly when \(\beta>n-3\).  When \(n=2\), the
corresponding integral is
\[
C\int_0^{\rho_0}\rho^\beta\log^2(e/\rho)\,d\rho,
\]
which is finite exactly when \(\beta>-1=n-3\).

Near an endpoint, the region \(s\geq0\) is covered by the preceding
estimate.  On the remaining region \(s<0\), put
\(s_-=-s\) and \(\delta=(s_-^2+|z|^2)^{1/2}\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left|
 \int_0^{|J|}
 \frac{f(t)}{((s-t)^2+|z|^2)^{(n-1)/2}}\,dt
 \right|^2
 \leq C\delta^{3-2n}\|f\|_2^2.
\]
Integration in the \(n\) variables \((s_-,z)\) again gives
\[
C\int_0^{\rho_0}\delta^{\beta+2-n}\,d\delta.
\]
Contributions from nonlocal pieces of the curve have bounded kernels.
They map \(L^2(ds_\Gamma)\) to \(L^2(\omega_\beta)\) because
\(\omega_\beta(U_{\rho_0})<\infty\).  The Green remainder has the same
property.  Summing the finitely many local estimates proves sufficiency.
The argument also bounds all tangent-line truncations uniformly, since
their multipliers are bounded by a fixed constant.

For \(n=2\), the assumed local finiteness condition is already
\(\beta>-1=n-3\).  We therefore prove necessity for \(n\geq3\).
Let \(\gamma\) be an
arc-length parametrization with \(\gamma(0)=0\), and put
\(N_0:=\gamma'(0)^\perp\).  After reducing \(r>0\), the map \((s,z)\longmapsto\gamma(s)+z, \quad (s,z)\in(-r,r)\times B_{N_0}(0,r)\), is one-to-one, its Jacobian is bounded above and below, and
\(d_\Gamma(\gamma(s)+z)\approx|z|\).  To see the first assertion,
project onto the line spanned by \(\gamma'(0)\).  The resulting scalar
function of \(s\) has derivative bounded away from zero.  The distance
comparison follows because \(\gamma'(s)\) remains close to
\(\gamma'(0)\).

Put \(\tau_s:=\gamma'(s)\) and
\(z_s:=z-(z\cdot\tau_s)\tau_s\).  Then \(|z_s|\approx|z|\).  After translating
the tangent variable by \(z\cdot\tau_s\), the normal part of the tangent
line integral is
\[
 -z_s\int_{-r+O(|z|)}^{r+O(|z|)}
 \frac{dt}{(t^2+|z_s|^2)^{n/2}}.
\]
Its absolute value is comparable to \(|z|^{2-n}\); changes at the two
finite endpoints are bounded.

Choose \(f\) equal to one on this subarc and supported on a slightly
larger arc.  Uniformly in \(s\), \(\gamma(s+t)-\gamma(s)=t\tau_s+E_s(t), \ |E_s(t)|\leq |t|\vartheta_\gamma(|t|)\). The difference between the curved kernel and the tangent-line kernel is
at most
\[
C\int_0^r
 \frac{t\vartheta_\gamma(t)}{(t^2+\rho^2)^{n/2}}\,dt,
 \qquad \rho:=|z|.
\]
A dyadic decomposition at \(t=\rho\) bounds this by
\[
C\rho^{2-n}
 \left(
  \vartheta_\gamma(\rho)
  +\sum_{\substack{k\geq0\\2^k\rho<r}}
   2^{-k(n-2)}\vartheta_\gamma(2^{k+1}\rho)
 \right).
\]
Choose \(r\) so small that the expression in parentheses is smaller
than the fixed tangent-line lower bound.  The part of the source outside the smaller arc and the Green remainder
are continuous across that arc.  The singular term tends to infinity,
so \(|\nabla u_f(\gamma(s)+z)|\geq c|z|^{2-n}\) for all small \(z\) and for \(s\) in a fixed shorter interval.  Integration in these coordinates gives
\[
 \int_{U_{\rho_0}}|\nabla u_f(x)|^2d_\Gamma(x)^\beta\,dx
 \geq c\int_0^{\rho_1}
 \rho^{4-2n}\rho^\beta\rho^{n-2}\,d\rho
 =c\int_0^{\rho_1}\rho^{\beta+2-n}\,d\rho.
\]
The last integral diverges when \(\beta\leq n-3\), with logarithmic
divergence at equality.  This proves necessity.

label: cor:whole-space-distance-power
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:whole-space-distance-power}
Let \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a compact regular
\(C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\) curve, let \(d\sigma=ds_\Gamma\), let
\(\beta>-(n-1)\), and put \(d\omega_\beta(x)=d_\Gamma(x)^\beta\,dx\). The whole-space estimate \(\|\mathbf R^{1,n}_{ds_\Gamma}f\|_{L^2(\omega_\beta)} \leq C_\beta\|f\|_{L^2(ds_\Gamma)}\) holds for every \(f\in L^2(ds_\Gamma)\) if and only if \(n-3<\beta<n-2\). For \(n=3\), the exact range is \(0<\beta<1\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof of \cref{cor:bounded-distance-power} gives the exact local
condition \(\beta>n-3\).  On a bounded set separated from \(\Gamma\),
the kernel and the weight are bounded.  Write
$|\Gamma|=\mathcal H^1(\Gamma)$ and put
\(M_\Gamma:=\sup_{y\in\Gamma}|y|\).  If \(|x|>2M_\Gamma+1\), then
\(d_\Gamma(x)\approx|x|\) and
\[
 |\mathbf R^{1,n}_{ds_\Gamma}f(x)|
 \leq C|x|^{1-n}
 \int_\Gamma|f|\,ds_\Gamma
 \leq C|x|^{1-n}|\Gamma|^{1/2}\|f\|_2.
\]
The square of this bound is integrable at infinity with respect to
\(d_\Gamma(x)^\beta dx\) exactly when
\[
 \int_1^\infty r^{\beta+1-n}\,dr<\infty,
\]
or \(\beta<n-2\).  This proves sufficiency.

For necessity at infinity, take \(f=1\).  A first-order expansion of the
kernel gives \(\mathbf R^{1,n}_{ds_\Gamma}1(x) =-c_{1,n}|\Gamma|\frac{x}{|x|^n}+O(|x|^{-n}) \quad\text{as }|x|\to\infty\). The leading term is nonzero.  Its weighted square integral diverges when
\(\beta\geq n-2\), logarithmically at equality.  For \(n\geq3\), the local lower bound in
the preceding proof gives necessity of \(\beta>n-3\).  For \(n=2\),
this condition follows from the assumed local finiteness.

label: cor:Biot-Savart
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Biot-Savart}
Let \(\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^3\) be a compact regular
\(C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}\) curve, let \(\sigma\) be a finite positive Borel
measure supported on \(\Gamma\), and let \(\omega\) be a locally finite
positive Borel measure on \(\mathbb R^3\).  Then
\[
 \sup_{0<\varepsilon<R}
 \|\mathcal B_{\varepsilon,R,\sigma}F\|_{L^2(\omega;\mathbb R^3)}
 \leq C\|F\|_{L^2(\sigma;\mathbb R^3)}
\]
holds for every vector density \(F\) if and only if the four
Muckenhoupt conditions and the forward and dual Riesz testing conditions
in \cref{thm:main}, with \(\alpha=1\), hold for \((\sigma,\omega)\).
The Biot--Savart operator norm is comparable to
\(\mathfrak N_{\mathbf R^{1,3}}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\varepsilon<R$, and write $\mathcal B_\sigma$ and
$\mathbf R_\sigma$ for the corresponding tangent-line truncated
Biot--Savart and $1$-fractional Riesz operators in $\mathbb R^3$.
Because the Riesz numerator is \(y-x\), while the Biot--Savart numerator is
\(F(y)\times(x-y)\), there is a nonzero dimensional constant \(c_B\)
such that, if \(F=\sum_{k=1}^3F_ke_k\), then
\[
 \mathcal B_\sigma F
 =c_B\sum_{k=1}^3e_k\times\mathbf R_\sigma F_k.
\]
Thus
\(\|\mathcal B_\sigma\|\leq
|c_B|\sqrt3\|\mathbf R_\sigma\|\).  Conversely,
apply \(\mathcal B_\sigma\) to \(fe_k\).  Since
\[
 \mathcal B_\sigma(fe_k)=c_Be_k\times\mathbf R_\sigma f,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k=1}^3|e_k\times v|^2=2|v|^2,
\]
we obtain \(2|c_B|^2\|\mathbf R_\sigma f\|_{L^2(\omega)}^2 \leq3\|\mathcal B_\sigma\|^2\|f\|_{L^2(\sigma)}^2\). These comparisons hold uniformly for the same truncations.  The result
now follows from \cref{thm:main}.
